ex.en: Applicants and their parents are said to believe that the personal essay can sway the admissions committee.
ex.zh: 据说，申请者和他们的父母相信，个人的论文会影响招生委员会的决定。

ex.en: The committee will publish its final recommendations on airport expansion early next month.
ex.zh: 委员会将于下月初发布关于机场扩建的最终建议。

ex.en: A special committee was set up to investigate the causes of the accident.
ex.zh: 人们成立了一个特别委员会来调查事故原因。

senses: n.[C] 商品；有使用价值的东西
n. 商品；有使用价值的东西
commodity.usage: [近] merchandise n. 商品；n.商品，货物；有用的东西；commodity 指可交易的初级产品/大宗商品；goods 泛指商品。；索引p404

ex.en: It was a year before she became head of a tiny Internet-based commodities exchange.
ex.zh: 一年后，她成了一家小型互联网商品交易所的负责人。

ex.en: Crude oil is a major commodity in international trade.
ex.zh: 原油是国际贸易中的大宗商品。

ex.en: Water has become a scarce and precious commodity in many parts of the world.
ex.zh: 在世界许多地区，水已成为稀缺而珍贵的商品。

ex.en: Heart disease is far more common among smokers than among non-smokers.
ex.zh: 心脏病在吸烟者中远比在非吸烟者中常见。

ex.en: The two countries must act in the common interest of regional stability.
ex.zh: 两国必须为了地区稳定这一共同利益采取行动。

ex.en: It is common knowledge that regular sleep improves memory and mood.
ex.zh: 众所周知，规律的睡眠能改善记忆和情绪。

ex.en: The study found a surprising commonality in how successful firms respond to crises.
ex.zh: 研究发现，成功企业应对危机的方式有着惊人的共性。

ex.en: Despite their differences, the two traditions share a striking commonality of purpose.
ex.zh: 尽管存在差异，这两种传统在目的上有着显著的共同点。

ex.en: Designers looked for commonalities across cultures before launching the global product.
ex.zh: 设计师在推出全球产品之前寻找跨文化的共同特征。

ex.en: It is commonly assumed that larger brains imply greater intelligence, but the evidence is far from conclusive.
ex.zh: 人们普遍认为更大的大脑意味着更高的智力，但相关证据远非定论。

commonplace.usage: 助记:common(共同的;普通的)+place(地方)→平凡

senses: n. [sing.]（政治上相联的国家集团的名称）联合体
n. 共和国,联邦,共同体
commonwealth.usage: [记] common（共同的）+wealth（富裕）→以共同富裕为目标的国家的集合→联合体；助记:common(共同的)+wealth(财富)→共和国

ex.en: Many small island economies still depend heavily on trade links within the Commonwealth.
ex.zh: 许多小型岛屿经济体仍在很大程度上依赖英联邦内部的贸易联系。

senses: adj. 公共的;公用的;群体的
adj. 社区的;团体的;公社制的
communal.usage: 词根记忆：com(together，一起)+mun(duty，义务)+al(与…有关的)→与一起承担义务有关的→团体的；索引p404

ex.en: The apartment block shares a communal garden where residents grow vegetables and hold summer gatherings.
ex.zh: 这栋公寓楼有一个公共花园，居民们在那里种菜并举办夏日聚会。

communicate.usage: com（共同）+muni（=many很多）+c+ate（动词后缀）→很多人共同在一起→交流，沟通；词根记忆：com(together，一起)+mun(duty，义务)+ic+ate(动词后缀)→使一起承担义务→共同探讨→交流；索引p404

ex.en: Language evolved as a means of communicating information between individuals.
ex.zh: 语言是作为个人之间交流信息的一种手段进化而来的。

ex.en: When your body language communicates reluctance or anxiety, it undercuts the message.
ex.zh: 当你的肢体语言传达出不情愿或焦虑时，你传达的信息就会被削弱。

ex.en: Managers must be able to communicate complex ideas clearly to non-specialists.
ex.zh: 管理者必须能够向非专业人员清晰地传达复杂想法。

ex.en: The two departments rarely communicated with each other, which led to duplicated work.
ex.zh: 两个部门之间很少沟通，导致工作重复。

ex.en: We need better communication with clients.
ex.zh: 我们需要与客户更好地沟通。

ex.en: Modern communication technologies have made remote work practical for millions of people.
ex.zh: 现代通信技术使数百万人远程办公成为可能。

ex.en: Poor communication between doctors and patients is a common cause of complaints.
ex.zh: 医患之间沟通不畅是引发投诉的常见原因。

ex.en: The storm disrupted communications across the entire region.
ex.zh: 风暴中断了整个地区的通信。

senses: n. 共产主义,共产主义学说,共产主义制度

ex.en: The exhibition traces how communism reshaped the region's industry, education and family life.
ex.zh: 这次展览追溯了共产主义如何重塑了该地区的工业、教育和家庭生活。

community.usage: commun（联想成common“共同的，公共的”）+ity（名词后缀，表示状态）→公共状态→社区，社会；词根记忆：com(together，一起)+mun(duty，义务)+ity(表物)→一起承担义务的机构→社区；团体；community service社区服务；索引p404

ex.en: Indeed, there is something a little absurd in the state getting involved in the planning of such a fundamentally "grassroots" concept as community sports associations.
ex.zh: 确实，让政府参与像社区体育协会这样从根本上带有“草根阶层”意味的规划是有些荒唐的。

ex.en: The astronomy community is making compromises to change its use of Mauna Kea.
ex.zh: 天文学界正在做出让步，以改变它对莫纳克亚山的占用。

ex.en: The new library has become a gathering place for the whole community.
ex.zh: 新图书馆已成为整个社区的聚集场所。

ex.en: The scientific community reacted cautiously to the unpublished findings.
ex.zh: 科学界对这份尚未发表的研究结果反应谨慎。

senses: v. 乘公交车辆上下班;通勤
v. 上下班往返，经常往返（于两地）
commute.usage: 派生commuter通勤者；com（共同，一起）+mute（=mote=move“移动，变换”）→大家一起移动→上下班往返；串词记忆：上下班往返(commute)时，我们经常一起交流(communicate)；索引p404

ex.en: I have only a short commute to work.
ex.zh: 我上班的路程很短。

ex.en: Rising fuel prices have pushed many workers to commute by train instead of by car.
ex.zh: 燃油价格上涨促使许多上班族改乘火车而非开车通勤。

ex.en: Her daily commute takes nearly two hours from door to door.
ex.zh: 她每天通勤从家门到单位门口要花近两个小时。

ex.en: The governor commuted the prisoner's sentence to the time already served.
ex.zh: 州长将这名囚犯的刑期减为已服刑期。

senses: n. （远距离）上下班往返的人
n.（远距离）上下班往返的人

ex.en: We need to encourage commuters not to drive into the city.
ex.zh: 我们需要鼓励通勤者不要开车进城。

senses: adj. 集中的,紧凑的,袖珍的
v. 使紧密结合,把……压实(或塞紧等)
compact.usage: com(一起)+pact(=pack压紧)→一起压紧→紧凑的，简洁的；索引p404

ex.en: The camera is compact enough to fit into a coat pocket.
ex.zh: 这台相机十分小巧，能放进外套口袋。

ex.en: The two sides signed a compact agreeing to share the region's water resources fairly.
ex.zh: 双方签署了一项公平共享该地区水资源的协议。

ex.en: Compact discs were once the dominant medium for recorded music.
ex.zh: 激光唱片曾是录制音乐的主要载体。

senses: n. 同伴,成双成对的物品之一

ex.en: He was a good friend, a dependable companion.
ex.zh: 他是个好朋友，一个可以信赖的同伴。

ex.en: Would passengers feel comfortable travelling in companion?
ex.zh: 旅客结伴旅行会感到舒服吗？

ex.en: She regarded her old dog as a loyal companion rather than a mere pet.
ex.zh: 她把自己的老狗视为忠实的伙伴，而不仅仅是宠物。

ex.en: For many elderly people living alone, a robotic companion can ease daily loneliness.
ex.zh: 对许多独居老人来说，机器人伙伴能缓解日常的孤独。

company.usage: 又:for company作为同伴,陪伴;in company of...在……陪同下；联想记忆：com(together,共同)+pan(平底锅)+y(名词后缀)→吃同一锅饭→公司；索引p404

ex.en: The company plans to hire two thousand graduates this year.
ex.zh: 该公司计划今年招聘两千名毕业生。

ex.en: She enjoys the company of colleagues who share her passion for research.
ex.zh: 她喜欢与和她一样热爱研究的同事为伴。

ex.en: He kept his grandfather company during the long winter evenings.
ex.zh: 在漫长的冬夜，他陪伴着祖父。

senses: adj. (常与 with 或 to 连用)可比较的，比得上的，类似的
adj. （数量、重要性等）相当的；类似的

ex.en: The two universities are comparable in size, reputation and research funding.
ex.zh: 这两所大学在规模、声誉和研究经费上不相上下。

ex.en: Prices here are far higher than in comparable towns nearby.
ex.zh: 这里的物价远高于附近条件相当的城镇。

ex.en: No comparable study has been carried out since the 1990s.
ex.zh: 自二十世纪九十年代以来，还没有进行过类似的研究。

senses: ②相比之下的，相比而言的，相对的
comparative.usage: n.比较级 adj.比较的；相对的；比较级 的；comparison 的派生词；索引p404

ex.en: The company is a comparative newcomer to the software market.
ex.zh: 就软件市场来说，这家公司相对而言就是新手了。

ex.en: The paper offers a comparative study of healthcare systems in five European countries.
ex.zh: 该论文对五个欧洲国家的医疗体系进行了比较研究。

ex.en: Following months of crisis, the region now enjoys a period of comparative stability.
ex.zh: 经过数月的危机，该地区目前处于相对稳定的时期。

phrases.m: 一段相对和平的早期历史

ex.en: Housing in the suburbs remains comparatively affordable for young families.
ex.zh: 郊区住房对年轻家庭来说仍相对便宜。

ex.en: The northern region is comparatively rich in natural resources.
ex.zh: 北部地区的自然资源相对丰富。

ex.en: Online courses are comparatively new, yet their influence on education is already profound.
ex.zh: 在线课程相对较新，但其对教育的影响已十分深远。

senses: v. ①(with, to) 比较，对照
compare.usage: 同义 match, contrast；compare to 比作，比拟；compare with 比较，可与……相比；v.比较，对比；把……比作；索引p404

ex.en: The data of an individual there gains its value only when it is compared with the data of countless millions more.
ex.zh: 现有的个人数据只有在与无数人的数据相比较时，才能获得自身价值。

ex.en: It is misleading to compare the two countries' growth rates without adjusting for inflation.
ex.zh: 不作通胀调整就比较两国增长率会产生误导。

ex.en: Children constantly compare themselves with their classmates.
ex.zh: 孩子们总是拿自己与同学作比较。

ex.en: Compared with last year, applications to engineering programmes have risen sharply.
ex.zh: 与去年相比，工程类专业的申请人数大幅上升。

senses: n. ①比较，对比，比喻，比拟

ex.en: The films are too different for a fair comparison.
ex.zh: 这些电影差异太大，无法进行公平的比较。

ex.en: In comparison with last year, the number of international visitors has risen by nearly twenty percent.
ex.zh: 与去年相比，国际游客人数增长了近百分之二十。

ex.en: A detailed comparison of the two proposals reveals sharp differences in cost.
ex.zh: 对两份提案的详细比较显示出两者在成本上的巨大差异。

senses: n. 卧车包房,(客车车厢内的)隔间
compartment.usage: 助记:com(共同)+part(分开)+ment(名词后缀)→隔间

ex.en: Even with satellite navigation, sailors are still taught to trust the compass first, because electronics can fail.
ex.zh: 即使有了卫星导航，水手们仍被教导要首先相信指南针，因为电子设备可能失灵。

compassion.usage: 助记:com(共同)+passion(感情)→共同的感情→同情;派生compassionate有同情心的；n.同情，怜悯；com（所有人）+passion（热情）→发生灾难时所有人都热情帮助，就是充满同情

ex.en: I felt no compassion towards her.
ex.zh: 我对她没有任何怜悯。

ex.en: Nurses need both technical skill and genuine compassion for their patients.
ex.zh: 护士既需要专业技能，也需要对病人真切的同情心。

ex.en: The charity appeals to the public's compassion for refugees displaced by war.
ex.zh: 该慈善机构呼吁公众对因战争流离失所的难民给予同情。

senses: adj. 有同情心的，表示怜悯的

ex.en: The hospice is widely praised for its compassionate care of terminally ill patients and their families.
ex.zh: 这家临终关怀医院因对绝症患者及其家属富有同情心的照料而广受赞誉。

senses: adj. 能共处的,合得来的
adj. 兼容的，可共用的，可共存的；（因思想、志趣等相投而）关系好的
compatible.usage: 助记:com(共同)+pat(忍受)→能共同忍受的;反义incompatible不相容；com(一起)+pat(拍)+ible→大家相互拍肩膀都是好朋友→关系好的

ex.en: Free enterprise, he argued, was compatible with Russian values and traditions.
ex.zh: 他认为自由企业与俄罗斯的价值观和传统是相容的。

ex.en: The new software is compatible with all major operating systems.
ex.zh: 新软件与所有主流操作系统兼容。

ex.en: The couple discovered their career ambitions were not compatible with family life.
ex.zh: 这对夫妇发现他们的职业抱负与家庭生活难以兼容。

compel.usage: com-（加强）+pel（推）→用力推→迫使。近义：force vt. 强迫；辨析：compel 强迫、迫使；impel 推动、驱使、激励、逼迫；词根记忆：com(together,一同)+pel(push,推)→大家一同推→迫使；索引p404

ex.en: The European Union is now considering legislation to compel corporate boards to maintain a certain proportion of women—up to 60 percent.
ex.zh: 欧盟正考虑立法，迫使公司董事会保持一定的女性比例——高达60%。

ex.en: Falling enrolment may compel the university to close two smaller departments.
ex.zh: 入学人数下降可能迫使这所大学关闭两个规模较小的系。

ex.en: The new regulations compel employers to publish data on pay differences.
ex.zh: 新规定迫使雇主公布薪酬差异数据。

ex.en: She felt compelled to speak out against the unfair decision.
ex.zh: 她觉得有必要对不公正的决定直言反对。

compensate.usage: com-（一起）+pens（称重量）→称出等重的→补偿。族：compensation n. 补偿。近义：make up for 弥补；offset 的近义词；同义 pay, reward, balance；派生 compensatory adj. 补(赔)偿的；com（所有的）+pens（花费）+ate（动词后缀）→把

ex.en: The fund will also be used to compensate landowners who set aside habitat.
ex.zh: 该基金也会被用于补偿那些主动留出栖息地的土地所有者。

ex.en: Work by Tina Malti, a psychology professor at the University of Toronto, suggests that guilt may compensate for an emotional deficiency.
ex.zh: 多伦多大学心理学教授蒂娜·马尔蒂的研究结果表明，内疚可以弥补情感上的缺失。

ex.en: Higher salaries do not fully compensate teachers for the pressure and long hours they face.
ex.zh: 更高的薪水并不能完全补偿教师所面临的压力和长时间工作。

compensation.usage: compensate 的派生词；n.赔偿金，补偿；报酬；索引p404

ex.en: Provide extra health compensation.
ex.zh: 提供额外的健康补偿。

ex.en: Victims of the delay are entitled to financial compensation under the contract.
ex.zh: 根据合同，因延误受损的一方有权获得经济补偿。

ex.en: Executives' compensation is increasingly linked to the company's long-term performance.
ex.zh: 高管薪酬日益与公司的长期业绩挂钩。

ex.en: The court ordered the firm to pay full compensation to the injured workers.
ex.zh: 法院责令该公司向受伤工人全额赔偿。

senses: a. 补偿的；赔偿的；补偿性质的

ex.en: Workers received compensatory payments for the extra hours they had worked.
ex.zh: 工人们因加班获得了补偿性报酬。

ex.en: The court awarded compensatory damages to the injured customers.
ex.zh: 法院判给受伤的顾客补偿性赔偿金。

ex.en: Schools in poor areas receive compensatory funding to narrow the achievement gap.
ex.zh: 贫困地区的学校获得补偿性拨款以缩小成绩差距。

senses: vi. 竞争；对抗；参加比赛（或竞赛）
v. 参加比赛；竞争，对抗

phrases.m: 为得到某物与某人竞争

compete.usage: [族]competition n. 竞争；competitor n. 竞争者；v.竞争，对抗；参加比赛；com(联想成company"公司")+pete(发音类似"PK")→公司之间PK，就是"竞争"；索引p404

ex.en: They are competing against teams of full-time professional players.
ex.zh: 他们正在与全职职业运动员团队竞争。

ex.en: For the time, attention, and money of the art-loving public, classical instrumentalists must compete not only with opera houses, dance troupes, theater companies, and museums, but also with the recorded performances of the great classical musicians of the 20th century.
ex.zh: 如今为了获得艺术爱好者的时间、关注和金钱，古典音乐演奏家们不仅要和歌剧院、舞蹈团、剧团和博物馆竞争，而且还需要和那些收录了20世纪伟大的古典音乐大师作品的唱片竞争。

ex.en: Small local shops struggle to compete with large chains on price and delivery speed.
ex.zh: 小型本地商店难以在价格和送货速度上与大型连锁店竞争。

ex.en: The assessment measures a student's competence in reading and reasoning rather than memory.
ex.zh: 该评估衡量的是学生阅读与推理方面的能力，而非记忆力。

ex.en: New employees must demonstrate competence before being allowed to work unsupervised.
ex.zh: 新员工必须先证明自己胜任工作，才能在无人监督的情况下上岗。

ex.en: Foreign policy falls outside the competence of local governments.
ex.zh: 外交政策超出了地方政府的职权范围。

senses: adj. ①有能力的，能胜任的
adj. 有能力的，足以胜任的
competent.usage: 派生 competently adv. 胜任地，适合地；adj.能胜任的；合格的，过得 去的；adj.能干的，能胜任的；合格的；索引p404

ex.en: Make sure the firm is competent to carry out the work.
ex.zh: 要确保这家公司有能力完成这项工作。

ex.en: In fact, it is difficult to see how journalists who do not have a clear grasp of the basic features of the Canadian Constitution can do a competent job on political stories.
ex.zh: 事实上，很难想象那些对加拿大宪法的基本特征缺乏清晰了解的新闻记者是如何胜任政治新闻报道工作的。

ex.en: A competent manager should recognize the early signs of conflict within the team.
ex.zh: 一名胜任的管理者应当能及早察觉团队内部冲突的迹象。

senses: adv. 足以胜任地，合格地

competition.usage: n.竞争；比赛；对手；词根记忆：com(together, 共同)+pet(seek, 追寻)+ition(名词后缀)→共同追寻同一样东西→竞争；索引p404

ex.en: The firm is facing stiff competition from its online rivals.
ex.zh: 该公司正面临来自在线竞争对手的激烈竞争。

ex.en: Competition law appears to be the only way to address these imbalances of power.
ex.zh: 竞争法似乎是唯一能解决这些权利失衡的办法。

ex.en: She entered the national writing competition and won first prize with a short story.
ex.zh: 她参加了全国写作比赛，并凭一篇短篇小说获得一等奖。

senses: adj. 竞争的；有竞争力的
adj. 竞争的，有竞争力的；一心求胜的
adj. 竞争的；求胜心切的
competitive.usage: adj.竞争的；好胜的；有竞争力的；索引p404

ex.en: When the competitive environment pushed our ancestors to achieve that potential, they could in turn afford more education.
ex.zh: 当竞争的环境促使我们的祖先获得这一潜力时，他们反过来又可以负担得起更多的教育。

ex.en: Graduates face an increasingly competitive job market as the number of applicants keeps rising.
ex.zh: 随着申请人数不断上升，毕业生面临竞争日益激烈的就业市场。

ex.en: The firm keeps its prices competitive by cutting advertising costs rather than wages.
ex.zh: 该公司通过削减广告开支而非工资来保持价格竞争力。

senses: n. 竞争者，对手；参赛者

ex.en: She is one of the sport's top competitors.
ex.zh: 她是这项运动成绩最好的选手之一。

ex.en: The airline cut fares to respond to a new low-cost competitor.
ex.zh: 这家航空公司降低票价，以应对新的低成本竞争对手。

ex.en: Firms that ignore their competitors' innovations risk losing market share.
ex.zh: 无视竞争对手创新的公司面临失去市场份额的风险。

compile.usage: com-（一起）+pil（堆）→堆在一起→汇编。近义：edit vt. 编辑；com-（一起）+pil（聚集）+e→将资料聚集在一起编成书→汇编；同义 collect；edit

ex.en: It took the research team three years to compile the data for the national survey.
ex.zh: 研究团队花了三年时间汇编这项全国性调查的数据。

complain.usage: com(所有)+p(联想people人)+lai(联想“赖”)+n(联想“你”)→大家都认为这事赖你→抱怨，埋怨

ex.en: American farmers have been complaining of labor shortages for several years.
ex.zh: 美国的农民这些年一直在抱怨劳动力不足。

ex.en: Residents complain that the new motorway has increased noise far beyond acceptable levels.
ex.zh: 居民抱怨新高速公路带来的噪音远远超出可接受的水平。

ex.en: Passengers complained about repeated delays, but the airline offered no explanation.
ex.zh: 乘客抱怨航班一再延误，但航空公司未作任何解释。

ex.en: Critics complain that the examination rewards memorisation over genuine understanding.
ex.zh: 批评者抱怨这场考试奖励死记硬背而非真正的理解。

ex.en: But there are few places where clients have more grounds for complaint than America.
ex.zh: 但是很少有地方可以像美国这样有更多的理由抱怨律师这个行业。

ex.en: The most common complaint from users concerns the software's complicated interface.
ex.zh: 用户最常见的抱怨是软件界面过于复杂。

ex.en: The council received dozens of complaints about the unreliable waste collection service.
ex.zh: 市政部门收到数十起对不可靠垃圾收集服务的投诉。

ex.en: A formal complaint must be submitted in writing within fourteen days.
ex.zh: 正式投诉必须在十四天内以书面形式提交。

complement.usage: 区别 compliment 赞美。完整的是 complementary；派生 complementary adj. 补充的，互补的；索引p404

ex.en: Online tutorials complement, rather than replace, the traditional classroom.
ex.zh: 在线辅导是对传统课堂的补充，而非取代。

ex.en: The wine was chosen to complement the main course.
ex.zh: 选这种酒是为了与主菜相配。

ex.en: We have a full complement of staff for the holiday season.
ex.zh: 我们为假期配备了全部所需的人员。

phrases.p: promote complementary and even competitive products
phrases.m: 推广互补性的，甚至竞争性的产品

complementary.usage: adj.互补的；相配的；词根记忆：com(表加强)+ple(fill,使充满)+ment(名词后缀)+ary(形容词后缀)→补充的；索引p404

ex.en: The two companies see their technologies as complementary rather than competing, which paved the way for the merger.
ex.zh: 这两家公司视彼此的技术为互补而非竞争，这为合并铺平了道路。

complete.usage: 派生 completely adv. 完全地，完整地，彻底地；adj.完全的；全部的；完成的 v.使完整；完成，结束

ex.en: The report is not complete; several key figures are still missing.
ex.zh: 报告还不完整，几项关键数据仍然缺失。

ex.en: Engineers expect to complete the bridge ahead of schedule.
ex.zh: 工程师们预计将提前建成这座大桥。

ex.en: It came as a complete surprise that the shop had closed overnight.
ex.zh: 那家店一夜之间关门，完全出乎人们的意料。

complex.usage: 派生 complexity n. 复杂性；adj.复杂的，难懂的 n.综合建筑群；复合体；词根记忆:com(together,一起)+plex(fold,折叠)→折叠到一起→复杂的;另:complex communication复杂的交流；索引p404

ex.en: We live in an increasingly complex world.
ex.zh: 我们生活在一个日益复杂的世界。

ex.en: Solving traffic congestion is a complex task that involves economics, engineering and human behavior.
ex.zh: 解决交通拥堵是一项复杂的任务，涉及经济学、工程学和人类行为。

ex.en: The old steel complex employed thousands of workers before it closed in the 1990s.
ex.zh: 这座老钢铁联合企业在二十世纪九十年代关闭前雇佣了数千名工人。

complexity.usage: n.复杂性；复杂之处；n.复杂性，错综复杂；索引p404

ex.en: The complexity of the tax code imposes heavy costs on small businesses without legal departments.
ex.zh: 税法的复杂性给没有法务部门的小企业带来了沉重成本。

compliance.usage: n.服从，遵守；词根记忆: com(thoroughly, 完全)+pli(fill, 满足)+ance→完全满足对方的条件→遵守；索引p404

ex.en: The factory was closed until it could prove compliance with safety rules.
ex.zh: 这家工厂被停业，直到能证明符合安全规定为止。

ex.en: New software helps firms monitor compliance with data protection laws.
ex.zh: 新软件帮助企业监督数据保护法的合规情况。

ex.en: Tax officials praised the company's full compliance with reporting requirements.
ex.zh: 税务官员称赞该公司完全遵守了申报要求。

senses: adj. 服从的，顺从的；一致的

ex.en: All new vehicles must be compliant with the tougher emission standards introduced this year.
ex.zh: 所有新车都必须符合今年实施的更严格排放标准。

complicate.usage: com（全部）+pli（折叠）+cate（表示形容词）→全部折叠的→使复杂化

ex.en: These events will greatly complicate the situation.
ex.zh: 这些事件将使局势变得极其复杂。

senses: adj. 错综复杂的，麻烦的
complicated.usage: intricate 的近义词；辨析：complicated 指众多部分、因素交织，难于分析理解；complex 指结构上的复杂，需高深知识才能理解；intricate 指盘根错节，难以掌握细节；adj.复杂的，难处理的；词根记忆:com(together,一起)+plic(fold,折叠)+ate(动词后缀)+(e)d

ex.en: The instructions were so complicated that most users gave up halfway through the installation.
ex.zh: 说明书太复杂，大多数用户安装到一半就放弃了。

ex.en: The legal process for adopting a child from abroad can be long and complicated.
ex.zh: 从国外收养儿童的法律程序可能漫长而复杂。

ex.en: The situation in the region is further complicated by long-running disputes over water resources.
ex.zh: 长期存在的水资源争端使该地区的局势更加复杂。

complication.usage: n.使复杂化的难题；并发症

ex.en: Bad weather added a further complication to a rescue operation already stretched to its limits.
ex.zh: 恶劣天气给本已捉襟见肘的救援行动又增添了一重困难。

compliment.usage: complement 补充；compliment 赞美；[族] complimentary a. 赞美的；[近] praise n./vt. 称赞（链P94）；vt.读['kɒmplɪment]；索引p404

ex.en: She accepted the compliment gracefully and thanked the audience.
ex.zh: 她优雅地接受了赞美，并向观众致谢。

ex.en: The chef complimented the young waiter on his excellent service.
ex.zh: 厨师称赞这位年轻服务员的服务非常出色。

ex.en: Paying customers a sincere compliment can improve their impression of a shop.
ex.zh: 真诚地赞美顾客能改善他们对商店的印象。

ex.en: Guests at the hotel receive complimentary breakfast and unlimited access to the fitness centre.
ex.zh: 酒店客人可享受免费早餐以及健身中心的无限次使用。

comply.usage: 近义：abide by / conform to 遵守；同义 conform, submit, obey；反义 refuse 拒绝；com（共同，一起）+ply（联想成play“玩”）→一起玩就要“遵守”规则，否则就乱套了→遵守。；comply with = conform to = abide by 遵守。；索引p4

ex.en: Companies must comply with the new regulations.
ex.zh: 公司必须遵守新规定。

ex.en: Those retailers may face headaches complying with various state sales tax laws.
ex.zh: 由于要遵守各种州内销售税法规，那些零售商可能会焦头烂额。

ex.en: Passengers who fail to comply with safety instructions may be refused travel.
ex.zh: 不遵守安全指示的乘客可能被拒绝乘坐。

senses: adj. (整体中的)一部分的,组成的
n. 组成部分,成分,部件
n. 组成部分；成分；部件
component.usage: n.组成部份，成分，部件 adj.组成的，构成的；索引p405

ex.en: Strength training is another important component of physical activity.
ex.zh: 力量训练是体育活动的另一个重要组成部分。

ex.en: Trust is an essential component of any successful working relationship.
ex.zh: 信任是任何成功的工作关系中不可或缺的组成部分。

ex.en: Each electronic component is tested twice before being installed in the final product.
ex.zh: 每个电子元件在装入成品前都要经过两次测试。

senses: v. 创作(音乐、文学作品),为……谱曲
v. 使(自己、思想等)准备好,使平静
v. 组成，构成；作曲；撰写

phrases.p: to compose a perfectly correct draft
phrases.m: 起草一份完全正确的草稿

compose.usage: 同义: make up, constitute; 反义: decompose；v.组成，构成；作曲；撰 写(信)；使平静；v.组成，构成；作曲；撰写(信)； 使平静；com(表示"都")+pose(姿势，摆姿势)→东西都放在一起摆成姿势→构成，组成→作曲；索引p405

ex.en: The earth is composed of several layers.
ex.zh: 地球由几层组成。

ex.en: Mozart composed his first symphony at the age of eight.
ex.zh: 莫扎特八岁时创作了他的第一部交响曲。

ex.en: Women compose nearly sixty percent of the students enrolled in the medical schools.
ex.zh: 在这些医学院注册的学生中，女性约占百分之六十。

senses: n. (尤指古典音乐的)创作者,作曲家
composer.usage: n.创作者，作曲家 / ˌ kɒmpə ˈ zɪʃ(ə)n/ 5 n.构成，成分；作品；作 曲；构图；作文

ex.en: The young composer blends folk melodies with modern electronic sounds.
ex.zh: 这位年轻作曲家把民间旋律与现代电子音效融合在一起。

ex.en: Mozart remains the most performed composer in concert halls worldwide.
ex.zh: 莫扎特仍是全球音乐厅中演奏次数最多的作曲家。

ex.en: Critics praised the film's score, calling its composer a major new talent.
ex.zh: 评论家称赞这部电影的配乐，称其作曲家是一位重要的新秀。

senses: adj. 合成的,复合的,混成的,集成的
n. 合成物;混合客车;综合照片;混合式(建筑物)

ex.en: The aircraft wings are built from lightweight composite materials.
ex.zh: 这种飞机机翼由轻质复合材料制成。

ex.en: Police released a composite sketch of the suspect based on witnesses' descriptions.
ex.zh: 警方根据目击者的描述公布了嫌疑人的合成素描像。

ex.en: The final index is a composite of several economic indicators.
ex.zh: 最终指数是若干经济指标的综合。

ex.en: The composition of the committee reflects a careful balance of regional interests.
ex.zh: 委员会的构成体现了各地区利益的审慎平衡。

ex.en: Students were asked to write a short composition on the advantages of city life.
ex.zh: 学生们被要求写一篇关于城市生活优点的短文。

ex.en: Scientists analysed the chemical composition of the ancient pottery fragments.
ex.zh: 科学家分析了古代陶器碎片的化学成分。

composure.usage: 易混辨析: calm强调镇静、平静的状态; composure强调能够保持镇静的个人能力；索引p405

ex.en: Composure is a state of mind made possible by the structuring of one's relation to one's environment.
ex.zh: 沉静是一种心态，当一个人与其周边的环境建立起关系时，才能拥有这种心态。

ex.en: She kept her composure even when the experiment failed for the third time.
ex.zh: 即使实验第三次失败，她也保持着镇定。

ex.en: The losing captain regained his composure before facing the press.
ex.zh: 落败的队长在面对媒体之前恢复了镇定。

senses: n. 复合物；混合物；复合词
v. 使加重；由……构成；混合
compound.usage: 助记:com+pound(放置)→使混合;辨析:blend混匀;integrate成整体；索引p405

ex.en: A compound sentence contains two or more clauses.
ex.zh: 复合句包含两个或多个从句。

ex.en: Water is a chemical compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
ex.zh: 水是氢和氧的化合物。

ex.en: Scientists combined several substances to create a new compound resistant to heat.
ex.zh: 科学家将数种物质结合，创造出一种耐热的新化合物。

ex.en: Compound interest allows savings to grow far faster over several decades.
ex.zh: 复利使储蓄在几十年间增长得快得多。

comprehend.usage: v.理解，领悟；词根记忆: com(completely, 彻底地)+prehend(seize, 抓住)→彻底地抓住→理解；索引p405

ex.en: Some philosophical texts are so abstract that even experts struggle to comprehend them.
ex.zh: 有些哲学文本过于抽象，连专家都难以理解。

ex.en: The scale of the disaster was too vast for the public to comprehend.
ex.zh: 灾难的规模之大超出公众的理解能力。

ex.en: Children can often comprehend a story long before they can read it themselves.
ex.zh: 孩子们往往在能够自己阅读之前很久就能听懂故事。

senses: n. 理解(力),了解;(听力或阅读)理解测试

ex.en: The reading passage was written at a level well beyond the comprehension of most beginners.
ex.zh: 这篇阅读文章的水平远远超出了大多数初学者的理解力。

ex.en: Listening comprehension improves fastest when learners hear the language in everyday situations.
ex.zh: 当学习者在日常情境中听到该语言时，听力理解提高得最快。

ex.en: The lecture was so technical that it defeated the comprehension of the general audience.
ex.zh: 这场讲座过于专业化，普通听众难以理解。

senses: adj. 广泛的,综合的;全部的;有理解力的
adj. 全部的，所有的；综合性的

ex.en: You are advised to take out comprehensive insurance.
ex.zh: 建议你购买综合保险。

ex.en: The report provides a comprehensive review of the evidence on remote working.
ex.zh: 该报告对远程办公的相关证据作了全面综述。

ex.en: The city has drawn up a comprehensive plan to cut traffic and improve air quality.
ex.zh: 该市制定了一个减少交通流量、改善空气质量的综合规划。

compress.usage: com(全部)+press(压)→全部压到一起→压缩

ex.en: Rehearsal time will have to be compressed into two evenings.
ex.zh: 排练时间将不得不压缩到两个晚上。

ex.en: New software compresses video files without any visible loss of quality.
ex.zh: 新软件能在没有明显画质损失的情况下压缩视频文件。

ex.en: The course compresses four years of study into eighteen intensive months.
ex.zh: 该课程把四年的学习压缩到十八个强化月中。

comprise.usage: comprise 与 consist of 表(整体)由……组成；compose 指(部分)构成整体，常用 be composed of；constitute 指(部分)构成整体；com(一起)+prise(联想成prize"奖赏")→一起奖赏，那就"包括"了所有人；索引p405

ex.en: The main labor force is comprised of students working part-time.
ex.zh: 主要的劳动力由兼职的学生组成。

ex.en: The committee comprises representatives from all six departments.
ex.zh: 委员会由来自全部六个部门的代表组成。

ex.en: The collection comprises more than two thousand paintings spanning five centuries.
ex.zh: 这批收藏包括两千多幅跨越五个世纪的画作。

ex.en: Women comprise nearly sixty percent of the university's current student body.
ex.zh: 女性占该大学现有学生总数的近百分之六十。

compromise.usage: com-(共同)+promis(允诺)→彼此许诺→互相让步→妥协；com(共同)+promise(承诺)→要双方都"妥协"才能达成共同的承诺→妥协；compromise 作动词还有“危害，损害”之意；make a compromise 做出让步。；①妥协例2008年阅读,②使陷入危险例2010年阅读:The detai

ex.en: The astronomy community is making compromises to change its use of Mauna Kea.
ex.zh: 天文学界在改变莫纳克亚山的用途方面作出妥协。

ex.en: After long talks, the two sides reached a compromise.
ex.zh: 经过长期谈判，双方达成了妥协。

ex.en: The incident compromised the company's reputation.
ex.zh: 这一事件损害了公司的声誉。

ex.en: Works of several historians reveal the moral compromises made by the nation's early leaders and the fragile nature of the country's infancy.
ex.zh: 几位历史学家的著作揭示了美国一些早期领导人所做出的那些道德上的妥协以及美国建国初期的脆弱本质。

ex.en: He felt a strong compulsion to check his phone every few minutes, even during meals.
ex.zh: 他有一种强烈的冲动，每隔几分钟就要看一眼手机，甚至在吃饭时也是如此。

senses: adj. 难以制止的；禁不住的
compulsive.usage: com-(加强)+puls(推)+-ive→不断推着做的→强迫性的；adj.难以抑制的，不能自拔的； 引人入胜的；索引p405

ex.en: It is unclear what luring was required, given his compulsive behavior.
ex.zh: 不清楚到底是什么样的诱惑使他做出这种强迫性行为。

ex.en: Compulsive shopping left him deep in debt within a year.
ex.zh: 强迫性购物使他在一年之内债台高筑。

ex.en: He was a compulsive gambler who borrowed money from friends and colleagues.
ex.zh: 他是一个难以自拔的赌徒，向朋友和同事四处借钱。

compulsory.usage: compuls(推)+-ory→必须推行的→强制的；[近] mandatory, obligatory；[近]obligatory a. 强制性的；辨析:compulsory依据法令强制执行;compulsive情不自禁的;反义voluntary自愿；索引p405

ex.en: Education is compulsory for children between six and fifteen in most countries.
ex.zh: 在大多数国家，六至十五岁的儿童必须接受义务教育。

ex.en: Wearing a helmet is compulsory for all motorcycle riders in the city.
ex.zh: 在该市，所有摩托车骑手都必须佩戴头盔。

ex.en: The union opposed the compulsory redundancy scheme proposed by management.
ex.zh: 工会反对管理层提出的强制裁员方案。

ex.en: Modern linguistics increasingly relies on computational methods to analyse vast collections of text.
ex.zh: 现代语言学日益依赖计算方法来分析海量文本。

compute.usage: 助记:com(全部)+pute(想)→全部想→估计

ex.en: The system can compute the optimal delivery route in less than a second.
ex.zh: 该系统能在不到一秒的时间内计算出最优配送路线。

ex.en: The museum displays an early computer the size of a room, capable of far less than a modern phone.
ex.zh: 博物馆展出了一台房间大小的早期计算机，其能力远不及一部现代手机。

senses: n. 计算；信息处理技术

ex.en: In his memoirs, the veteran recalls the comrade who saved his life during the final assault.
ex.zh: 在回忆录中，这位老兵回忆了在最后总攻中救了他一命的战友。

senses: vt. 隐藏；隐瞒（信息）；掩饰（情感）
conceal.usage: 【记】他隐瞒了自己的真实身份。反reveal vt.揭露；助记:con(全部)+ceal(隐藏)→全部隐藏→隐藏；conceal...from... 向…隐瞒；比 hide 更正式。；词根:con(表强调)+ceal(hide藏)→隐藏;同根词根ceal=to hide藏;vt.隐藏例为2021年阅读；索引p405

ex.en: He concealed his disappointment from his friends.
ex.zh: 他对朋友们隐瞒了自己的失望。

ex.en: Nature gave us lips to conceal our teeth.
ex.zh: 大自然赋予了我们嘴唇以隐藏牙齿。

ex.en: Firms cannot legally conceal safety records from their regulators.
ex.zh: 公司从法律上不得向监管机构隐瞒安全记录。

senses: v. 承认某事属实、有效、合理等
v. 承认自己输掉(一局、一次竞选等)
v. （不情愿地）承认；让步，认输
concede.usage: 助记:con(全部)+cede(放弃)→全部放弃→将(某物)让出；v.承认；让与；con（都）+cede（走）→都走了→承认；让步；concede 承认（不情愿）；admit 承认（一般用词）。；索引p405

ex.en: He reluctantly conceded the point to me.
ex.zh: 他不情愿地向我承认了这一点。

ex.en: He finally conceded that he was wrong.
ex.zh: 他最终承认自己错了。

ex.en: The new treatment could conceivably cut recovery times in half.
ex.zh: 新疗法有可能把恢复时间缩短一半。

ex.en: Prices could not conceivably rise much further without hurting demand.
ex.zh: 价格再不可能大幅上涨而不损害需求。

ex.en: Conceivably, the court might delay its ruling until after the election.
ex.zh: 法院有可能把裁决推迟到选举之后。

conceive.usage: con-（一起）+ceiv（拿）→拿到一起→构想。族：concept n. 概念。近义：imagine vt. 想象；[族]concept n. 概念；conceive 构思、想象；deceive 欺骗；perceive 发觉、理解；receive 收到、受到；con（共同；一起）+ceive（抓住）→一起去抓住思想→

ex.en: Most parents of soccer fans would like to conceive their babies in spring.
ex.zh: 很多球迷父母更愿意在春季孕育他们的孩子。

ex.en: It is difficult to conceive of a modern economy functioning without digital payments.
ex.zh: 很难设想没有数字支付的现代经济如何运转。

ex.en: The architect conceived the building as a bridge between the old town and the harbour.
ex.zh: 建筑师将这座建筑构想为连接老城与港口的桥梁。

ex.en: She could not conceive that anyone would object to such a reasonable plan.
ex.zh: 她无法想象会有人反对如此合理的计划。

concentrate.usage: con-(共同)+centr(中心)+ate→向中心聚→集中；[族] concentration n. 专心；浓度；con（所有）+centr（联想成 centre 中心）+ate（动词后缀）→左右中心都放到一个地方→集中；索引p405

ex.en: When we travel down a well-known route, because we don't have to concentrate much, time seems to flow more quickly.
ex.zh: 当我们沿着熟悉的路线旅行时，因为我们不必太集中精力，时间似乎过得更快。

ex.en: Ms. Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it "controlled" the data and DeepMind merely "processed" it.
ex.zh: 德纳姆女士将主要责任归咎于英国国民健康服务(NHS)基金会，因为在现行法律之下，它“掌控”数据，而深度思想公司只是“处理”数据。

ex.en: Unable to concentrate on her book, she kept glancing at the phone on the desk.
ex.zh: 她无法集中注意力看书，不停地瞟着桌上的手机。

concentration.usage: n.专心，专注；集中，聚集； 浓度；索引p405

ex.en: Constant notifications destroy the concentration that deep work requires.
ex.zh: 不停的消息提醒破坏了深度工作所需的专注力。

ex.en: The concentration of wealth in a few hands worries many economists.
ex.zh: 财富集中在少数人手中令许多经济学家担忧。

ex.en: The test measures the concentration of lead in the drinking water.
ex.zh: 该测试测量饮用水中铅的浓度。

concept.usage: conceive 的派生词；New Concept English《新概念英语》我们很熟悉，那 concept 就是“概念”。；词根:con(together一起)+cept(take拿)→把所有细节一起抓住提炼→概念；索引p405

ex.en: They radically changed people's concept of beauty.
ex.zh: 他们从根本上改变了人们对美的观念。

ex.en: Privacy law builds on the concept of damage to an individual from identifiable knowledge about them.
ex.zh: 隐私法建立在以个体可识别信息对个体造成伤害的概念上。

ex.en: The concept of fairness means different things in different cultures.
ex.zh: 公平这一概念在不同的文化中有不同的含义。

senses: n. ①概念，观念，主意，计划，意图(c/u)
conception.usage: n.概念，观念；构想；受孕；易混词辨析:concept指对某事物是什么、怎么做等的想法,通常指抽象概念;conception指对某事物的大致理解,侧重概括性；索引p405

ex.en: Different people have different conceptions.
ex.zh: 不同的人有不同的理解。

ex.en: This top-down conception of the fashion business couldn't be more out of date.
ex.zh: 这种自上而下的时尚行业理念已经完全过时了。

ex.en: The public conception of the scientist as a lonely genius is largely a myth.
ex.zh: 公众把科学家视为孤独天才的印象在很大程度上是一种虚构。

senses: adj. 概念（上）的；观念（上）的

concern.usage: con-(共同)+cern(分开)→把分开的归到一起→与……有关→涉及；n.担心，忧虑；关心；重要的 事物 v.关于；涉及，影响；使担心；索引p405

ex.en: Another nationwide concern is whether public funds from other agencies are going into construction in fire-prone districts.
ex.zh: 另一个国民关注的问题是：其他机构的公共资金是否会用于森林火灾高发地区的建设。

ex.en: Safety concerns delayed the launch of the new aircraft by two years.
ex.zh: 安全方面的担忧使新飞机的启用推迟了两年。

ex.en: The report is chiefly concerned with the impact of automation on low-skilled jobs.
ex.zh: 这份报告主要涉及自动化对低技能岗位的影响。

ex.en: Parents expressed growing concern about the amount of screen time in schools.
ex.zh: 家长们对学生在校使用电子屏幕的时间表示日益担忧。

senses: adj. 担心的；关注的；相关的
concerned.usage: adj.相关的；担心的；关心的；索引p405

ex.en: He was not interested in daily politics, but concerned with questions of moral behavior and the larger questions of right and wrong affecting the entire society.
ex.zh: 他对日常政治不感兴趣，但关注道德行为问题以及影响全社会的更大的是非问题。

concert.usage: 助记:con(一起)+cert(sert加入)→音乐家一起加入的盛会→音乐会

ex.en: The open-air concert attracted an audience of more than twenty thousand despite the rain.
ex.zh: 尽管下着雨，这场露天音乐会仍吸引了两万多名观众。

senses: n. 让步，妥协；承认，许可
concession.usage: 记：con-（加强意义）+cess（退让）+-ion（名词后缀）→做出的退让→让步；助记:con(共同)+cess(走,让步)+ion(后缀)→共同屈服→让步；n.让步，妥协；特许；索引p405

ex.en: The company will be forced to make concessions to the union.
ex.zh: 公司将被迫向工会作出让步。

ex.en: After weeks of talks, the union won a major concession on working hours.
ex.zh: 经过数周谈判，工会在工作时间问题上赢得了一项重大让步。

ex.en: As a concession to local residents, the company agreed to reduce nighttime construction noise.
ex.zh: 作为对当地居民的让步，该公司同意降低夜间施工噪音。

senses: a. （尤指词典）简明的，简缩的
adj. 简明的，简洁的；简练的
concise.usage: 记：con-（加强意义）+cis（切）+e→剪切掉冗余部分→简洁的；con（一起、共同）+cise（切；杀）→一起切掉，全部切掉，就很简洁了→简明的，简洁的

ex.en: Make your answers clear and concise.
ex.zh: 回答要清晰简洁。

ex.en: Good abstracts are concise yet cover the paper's main findings.
ex.zh: 好的摘要简洁明了，又涵盖论文的主要发现。

ex.en: The manual gives concise instructions for installing the machine.
ex.zh: 说明书提供了安装机器的简明指引。

conclude.usage: con-(共同)+clud(关闭)→一起关闭→结束→得出结论；[族] conclusion；infer 的近义词；con（表示“所有的”）+clude（=close，关上）→所有的都关上了→结束；得出结论；词根记忆：con(together,全部)+clud(shut,关闭)+e→全部关掉→结束；索引p405

ex.en: It is too early for us to conclude anything.
ex.zh: 我们现在下结论还为时过早。

ex.en: With the use of eye-tracking technology, Julia Minson of the Harvard Kennedy School of Government concluded that eye contact can signal very different kinds of messages, depending on the situation.
ex.zh: 哈佛大学肯尼迪政府学院的朱丽娅·明森利用眼球追踪技术得出结论：在不同情景下，眼神交流能够传递截然不同的信息。

ex.en: The researchers concluded that moderate exercise significantly reduces the risk of heart disease.
ex.zh: 研究人员得出结论，适度运动能显著降低患心脏病的风险。

phrases.m: (未经全面考虑)匆匆作出结论

ex.en: Its conclusion is purposely exaggerated.
ex.zh: 它的结论被故意夸大了。

ex.en: The researchers were careful not to draw conclusions from incomplete data.
ex.zh: 研究人员谨慎地避免从不完整的数据中得出结论。

ex.en: In conclusion, the author calls for greater investment in rural healthcare.
ex.zh: 在结尾处，作者呼吁加大对农村医疗的投入。

ex.en: The peace treaty brought the eight-year conflict to a conclusion.
ex.zh: 和平条约为长达八年的冲突画上了句号。

conclusive.usage: adj.结论性的，毫无疑问的， 确定的；索引p405

ex.en: There is no conclusive evidence that it causes cancer in humans.
ex.zh: 没有确凿的证据表明它会导致人类患癌。

ex.en: The study offers conclusive proof that the drug reduces blood pressure.
ex.zh: 该研究为这种药物能降血压提供了确凿的证明。

ex.en: Without conclusive data, scientists refused to announce a formal discovery.
ex.zh: 由于缺乏确凿数据，科学家拒绝宣布正式发现。

senses: v. 用混凝土修筑，浇混凝土
concrete.usage: concrete 是与抽象相对的具体，指可通过感官看到、听到、触到；specific 是与一般、模糊相对的具体；adj.确实的，具体的 n.混凝土；con(一起，共同)+crete(联想create"创造")→一起努力创造"具体的"未来→具体的；词根:con(together共同)+cre(create生长)+te→长

ex.en: I liked facts, things that are concrete.
ex.zh: 我喜欢事实，喜欢具体的东西。

ex.en: But under anti-bribery laws, proof must be made of concrete benefits, such as approval of a contract or regulation.
ex.zh: 但是依照反贿赂法，证据必须是获得了实际好处，比如签署一份合同或获批一项法规。

ex.en: The proposal remains vague and offers no concrete plans for reducing costs.
ex.zh: 该提案仍然含糊其辞，没有提出削减成本的具体计划。

senses: v. 同意,赞同;意见一致
adj. 并存的，同时发生的
vt. 宣告(某人)有罪,判刑

phrases.p: condemn the players for lack of ability
condemn sb. for sth. / to do sth.
phrases.m: 因某事谴责某人 / 判某人做某事

condemn.usage: 记：con-（加强意义）+demn（惩罚）→法官宣布处以某种惩罚→判处；辨析: condemn 声讨、谴责、惩罚,尤指道义上谴责,语气重; scold 责骂,直接言语责备; blame 责备、归咎; censure 责难,上级对下级,较正式; 反义: excuse；demn发音类似damn（电影中经常听到的咒骂语），那

ex.en: But while this may be true, it's not a good enough reason to condemn gap years.
ex.zh: 但是即便如此，这也不是一个足够谴责间隔年的好理由。

ex.en: World leaders condemned the attack as a crime against civilians.
ex.zh: 世界各国领导人谴责这次袭击是针对平民的罪行。

ex.en: The prisoner was condemned to ten years in prison for fraud.
ex.zh: 该囚犯因诈骗罪被判处十年监禁。

ex.en: Critics condemned the decision as short-sighted and damaging to the region.
ex.zh: 批评者谴责这一决定目光短浅，损害该地区利益。

senses: v. 压缩，简编；浓缩；冷凝，凝结
condense.usage: 记：con-（加强意义）+dens（浓）+e→使汤越来越浓→使变浓；同义: compress, concentrate; 反义: expand；v.凝结；压缩；浓缩；con(所有)+dense(稠密)→使所有的部分变得稠密→压缩

ex.en: Steam condenses on cold windows during the winter months.
ex.zh: 冬季，水蒸气在冰冷的窗户上凝结。

ex.en: The editor asked her to condense the 300-page manuscript into a single article.
ex.zh: 编辑请她将三百页的手稿压缩成一篇文章。

ex.en: She condensed her argument into three clear points for the final presentation.
ex.zh: 在最终陈述中，她把论点精简为清晰的三点。

senses: n. 状态，状况；环境；条件
condition.usage: n.状况，状态；条件；疾病 v.训练，使习惯于；影响；索引p405

ex.en: Travellers on the Silk Road faced the possibility of being attacked by thieves or being subjected to extreme weather conditions.
ex.zh: 丝绸之路上的旅行者面临着可能被盗贼袭击或遭遇极端天气情况。

ex.en: The old bridge is in poor condition and requires urgent repairs.
ex.zh: 这座老桥状况糟糕，急需维修。

ex.en: The company accepted the merger on condition that it control the new board.
ex.zh: 该公司接受了合并，条件是由它控制新董事会。

ex.en: Economic conditions in the region have improved steadily since the reform.
ex.zh: 改革以来，该地区的经济状况稳步改善。

ex.en: The bank's support remains conditional on the company meeting strict quarterly targets.
ex.zh: 银行的支持仍以公司达到严格的季度目标为前提。

conditioner.usage: n.护发素；衣物柔顺剂；调节 剂，调节器

senses: n. [U] 行为；举止；经营方式
conduct.usage: 注意 conduct 作名词和动词时读音不同：/'kɒndʌkt/ n.；/kənˈdʌkt/ v.；con(共同)+duct(引导；带来)→引导大家共同做→指挥；词根:con(together共同)+duct(lead引导)→引导大家一起做→引导;①v.实施例为2020年阅读;②n.举止(2012年完形):At th

ex.en: The school board is responsible for conducting public hearings.
ex.zh: 校董会负责组织公开的听证会。

ex.en: A UK-based brand manager conducts regular 60-day surveys of British youth.
ex.zh: 一家英国品牌的经理定期对英国年轻人进行60天的调查。

ex.en: The company was criticised for the conduct of its senior managers.
ex.zh: 该公司因高管的行为而受到批评。

ex.en: Scientists conducted a series of experiments to test the hypothesis.
ex.zh: 科学家进行了一系列实验来检验这一假设。

senses: n. (电车等的)售票员,列车员
n. 指挥；售票员，检票员；导体
n. （交响乐、合唱的）指挥；导体；领导者；售票员；列车长

ex.en: The conductor raised his baton and the orchestra began to play.
ex.zh: 指挥举起指挥棒，乐团开始演奏。

ex.en: Copper is widely used in electric cables because it is an excellent conductor.
ex.zh: 铜是优良的导体，因此被广泛用于电缆。

ex.en: Passengers on the old trains bought tickets from the conductor during the journey.
ex.zh: 乘坐旧式列车的乘客在旅途中向列车员购票。

senses: v. 授予，赋予；商讨；协商；交换意见
confer.usage: 在大会（conference）上授予（confer）某人奖项（或者“商讨”事情）。；索引p405

ex.en: That compulsion has resulted in robotics—the science of conferring various human capabilities on machines.
ex.zh: 那种冲动导致了机器人技术的出现，这是一门将人类的各种能力赋予机器的科学。

ex.en: The university confers honorary degrees on leading figures in science and the arts each year.
ex.zh: 该大学每年向科学界和艺术界的领军人物授予荣誉学位。

ex.en: The board conferred for hours before announcing its final decision on the merger.
ex.zh: 董事会商议了数小时才宣布对合并的最终决定。

conference.usage: n.(大型、正式的)会议，研讨 会；体育协会

ex.en: The annual conference brings together researchers from more than thirty countries.
ex.zh: 年会汇聚了来自三十多个国家的研究人员。

ex.en: He is attending a conference on climate policy in Geneva this week.
ex.zh: 他本周正在日内瓦出席一场气候政策会议。

ex.en: Details of the plan were first announced at a press conference.
ex.zh: 该计划的细节最初是在一次新闻发布会上公布的。

senses: v. 供认，承认，坦白；忏悔
confess.usage: admit 指屈服于外力或受良心驱使而承认；confess 指坦白、忏悔，常指对本身不利或犯罪事实的承认；con（一起、全部）+fess（=speak，表示“说”）→全部说出来→承认、坦白。派生：confession；confess to doing sth；confession n. 供认，忏悔。

ex.en: She confessed to the murder.
ex.zh: 她供认犯了谋杀罪。

ex.en: He confessed to stealing the money.
ex.zh: 他承认偷了钱。

ex.en: After hours of questioning, the suspect confessed to the crime.
ex.zh: 经过数小时讯问，嫌疑人对罪行供认不讳。

ex.en: I must confess that I have never read the original novel.
ex.zh: 我必须承认，我从未读过这部小说的原著。

ex.en: After months of denial, the suspect's confession finally brought the two-year investigation to a close.
ex.zh: 在数月否认之后，嫌疑人的供认终于使这场为期两年的调查画上句号。

senses: n. 知心朋友,知己,密友
n. 信任,信心,自信,把握
n. 私下里说的话,秘密话

ex.en: It may be a well-researched opinion, but it's still an opinion, so talk tentatively and slightly understate your confidence.
ex.zh: 它(指你的观点)可能是一个经过对相关情况充分了解、充分调研的观点，但它仍然只是一个观点，所以探讨性地地说你的观点并且稍微低调一点。

ex.en: Repeated failures undermined her confidence in her own judgement.
ex.zh: 一再的失败动摇了她对自己判断力的信心。

ex.en: The central bank's statement was intended to restore investor confidence.
ex.zh: 央行的声明旨在恢复投资者信心。

ex.en: He answered every question with complete confidence during the interview.
ex.zh: 面试中他信心十足地回答了每一个问题。

confident.usage: 记 con-(加强意义)+fid(相信)+-ent(形容词后缀)→相信自己的→自信的；反 uncertain；索引p405

ex.en: The teacher wants the children to feel confident about asking questions when they don't understand.
ex.zh: 教师要孩子们遇到不懂的就大胆提问。

ex.en: Analysts are confident that the economy will recover by the end of the year.
ex.zh: 分析师确信经济将在年底前复苏。

ex.en: She felt confident of winning the contract after the successful demonstration.
ex.zh: 演示成功后，她坚信自己能赢得这份合同。

ex.en: A confident manner can be as important as solid preparation in a job interview.
ex.zh: 在求职面试中，自信的态度与扎实的准备同样重要。

ex.en: Companies need to impose restrictions on confidential information.
ex.zh: 公司需要对机密信息施加限制。

ex.en: Employees must not discuss confidential company documents outside the office.
ex.zh: 员工不得在办公室外讨论公司机密文件。

ex.en: Medical records are strictly confidential and cannot be shared without consent.
ex.zh: 病历严格保密，未经同意不得共享。

senses: n. 布局,结构,构造,格局,形状

confine.usage: con-（加强）+fin（界限）→给出界限→限制。近义：limit vt. 限制；辨析: confine 限制在狭窄范围内或禁闭,常与 to/within 连用; bound 形成界线、限制,常用被动; control 通过权力和影响监督控制; restrain 感情上的抑制、束缚,常与 from 连用；v.限制，局限

ex.en: These small mammals are generally confined to the south of the island.
ex.zh: 这些小型哺乳动物一般只出没于该岛南部。

ex.en: The discussion should not be confined to economic issues alone.
ex.zh: 讨论不应仅局限于经济问题。

ex.en: The patient was confined to bed for six weeks after the operation.
ex.zh: 手术后，病人卧床六周。

senses: vt. (尤指提供证据来)确认，证实
vt. 巩固(地位、角色或权力)
vt. 确定，确认(安排或预约)
confirm.usage: 记 con-(加强意义)+firm(确定)→确定；族 confirmation n. 确认书；近 verify vt. 证实；同义: prove, verify; 反义: disprove；con（表示"加强"）+firm（坚定的）→使坚定→证实；词根记忆：con(表加强)+firm(strong,坚固的)→使坚固→确

ex.en: But today a man can boost his paternal (fatherly) wisdom—or at least confirm that he's the kid's dad.
ex.zh: 但是如今男人可以提升自己作为父亲的智慧——至少可以确认自己是孩子的父亲。

ex.en: It is a wise father that knows his own child, but today a man can boost his paternal (fatherly) wisdom—or at least confirm that he's the kid's dad.
ex.zh: 即使再聪明的父亲也未必了解自己的孩子。但如今男人可以提升其为人父的智慧，或者至少能确认自己是这个孩子的父亲。

ex.en: The experiment confirmed his theory.
ex.zh: 实验证实了他的理论。

conflict.usage: 辨析: conflict 敌对双方斗争或内部矛盾; contest 友谊性竞赛或带敌意的争斗; combat 格斗或遭遇战; fight 个人或象征性冲突,与逆境的抗争; 反义: agreement；n.争执，争论，分歧；矛 盾 v.冲突，抵触；真题词组:ease conflicts between races and

ex.en: The results of the new research would seem to conflict with existing theories.
ex.zh: 这项新研究的结果似乎与现有的理论相冲突。

ex.en: The new airport plan brought the government into conflict with environmental groups.
ex.zh: 新机场计划使政府与环保团体发生了冲突。

ex.en: Their accounts of the accident conflict sharply on one key detail.
ex.zh: 他们对事故的叙述在一个关键细节上大相径庭。

conform.usage: comply 的近义词；conform 与 to 或 with 连用，意为符合或遵守公认的规则、准则；v.遵守；顺从，随潮流；一致， 相吻合；con（共同）+form（形式）→共同的形式→相一致；conform to 符合/遵守；conformity n. 一致。；索引p405

ex.en: He refused to conform to the local customs.
ex.zh: 他拒绝遵从当地的风俗习惯。

ex.en: The products conform to international safety standards.
ex.zh: 这些产品符合国际安全标准。

ex.en: All new buildings must conform to strict energy-efficiency standards.
ex.zh: 所有新建筑都必须符合严格的能效标准。

senses: n. （对社会规则的）遵从，遵守；（in ~with/to）符合，一致
n. 随大流；（对社会规则的）遵从，遵守
conformity.usage: n.遵守，依照；符合，一致；索引p405

ex.en: It was in conformity to the prevailing practice in the market.
ex.zh: 这符合市场的普遍做法。

ex.en: Products sold in the EU must be in conformity with its safety standards.
ex.zh: 在欧盟销售的产品必须符合其安全标准。

ex.en: Teenagers often feel pressure towards conformity in dress and behaviour.
ex.zh: 青少年常常感到在衣着和行为上随大流的压力。

confront.usage: con-（一起）+front（前面）→来到面前→面对。近义：face vt. 面对；con(一起)+front(前面)→都到前面来了，一起面对困难→面对；词根:con(together共同)+front(face面对)→共同面对→正视（困难或问题）；索引p405

ex.en: He is willing to confront problems directly.
ex.zh: 他愿意直接面对问题。

ex.en: In fact, the ability to maintain emotional control when confronted by stress is one of the most significant of all life's skills.
ex.zh: 事实上，面对压力时控制情绪的能力是所有生活技能中最重要的技能之一。

ex.en: Coastal cities must confront the growing threat of rising sea levels.
ex.zh: 沿海城市必须应对海平面上升带来的日益严峻的威胁。

ex.en: Diplomats managed to defuse the confrontation before it escalated into open conflict.
ex.zh: 外交官们在对峙升级为公开冲突之前成功化解了危机。

senses: v. 使糊涂；使困惑；（将……）混淆，混同
confuse.usage: con（共同）+fus（流）+e→流到一起→（将……）混淆；索引p405

ex.en: These two sets of statistics are guaranteed to confuse the public.
ex.zh: 这两套统计数据肯定会把公众搞糊涂。

ex.en: Do not confuse correlation with causation when interpreting survey data.
ex.zh: 解读调查数据时，不要把相关性误当作因果关系。

ex.en: The similar names of the two roads confuse visitors, who often end up in the wrong place.
ex.zh: 两条路名字相近，游客常常因此走错地方。

ex.en: History and news become confused, and one's impressions tend to be a mixture of skepticism and optimism.
ex.zh: 历史事件和新闻发生混淆，人们对于大众媒体的感受往往掺杂着怀疑和乐观。

senses: adj. 令人困惑的；难以理解的

ex.en: Tourists often find the timetable confusing, since two different companies operate trains on the same line.
ex.zh: 游客常常觉得这份时刻表令人困惑，因为同一条线路上有两家不同的公司在运营火车。

senses: n. 混乱局面；混淆；困惑
n. 混乱；困惑；不确定；混淆
confusion.usage: n.困惑；混淆；窘迫；混 乱局面；索引p405

ex.en: To avoid confusion, the two similar products were given clearly different names.
ex.zh: 为避免混淆，这两款相似的产品被赋予了明显不同的名称。

ex.en: There was widespread confusion after the sudden change in the rules was announced.
ex.zh: 突然宣布更改规则后，出现了普遍的混乱。

ex.en: Her explanation only added to the confusion rather than resolving it.
ex.zh: 她的解释不但没有澄清问题，反而加深了困惑。

senses: n. 联合大企业,企业集团

phrases.m: 就某事向某人表示祝贺

ex.en: Letters of congratulation poured in from around the world after the team's historic victory.
ex.zh: 球队取得历史性胜利后，来自世界各地的贺信纷至沓来。

senses: n. (代表)大会；(C-)(美国等国的)国会，议会
n. 国会，议会；代表大会
congress.usage: n.国会；代表大会；con（共同，一起）+gress（走）→走到一起开会→国会；词根记忆:con(together,一起)+gress(go,走)→走到一起(开会)→代表大会;易混:大写Congress指美国国会,parliament大写指英国议会；索引p405

ex.en: Congress will vote on the proposals tomorrow.
ex.zh: 国会明天将对提案进行表决。

ex.en: After a bruising encounter with Congress, America's Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) rushed through rule changes.
ex.zh: 在与国会的交锋挫败之后，美国财务会计标准委员会(FASB)匆忙通过了对准则的修改。

ex.en: The bill was narrowly approved by Congress after months of debate.
ex.zh: 经过数月辩论，该法案在国会以微弱优势获得通过。

ex.en: An international congress of scientists will be held in Kyoto next spring.
ex.zh: 明年春天将在京都举行国际科学家代表大会。

senses: adj. 国家立法机关的,议会的

ex.en: The congressional committee has demanded internal documents relating to the failed merger.
ex.zh: 国会委员会已要求提供与这场失败合并相关的内部文件。

conjunction.usage: 派生conjunctional连接的;助记:con(共同)+junct(连接)+ion→连接；词根记忆:con(together,一起)+junct(join,结合)+ion→结合在一起→结合；索引p405

ex.en: The new drug is most effective when used in conjunction with a carefully controlled diet.
ex.zh: 这种新药与严格控制饮食配合使用时效果最佳。

connect.usage: 词根记忆：con(表加强)+nect(link, 连接)→把…联系起来；索引p405

ex.en: You're more likely to be heard if you can connect your disagreement to a higher purpose.
ex.zh: 如果你能把你的异议和更高的目标联系起来，你的意见更有可能会被听取。

ex.en: The new high-speed rail will connect eight major cities along the coast.
ex.zh: 新高铁将连接沿海八座大城市。

ex.en: Good teachers connect abstract theory to problems students meet every day.
ex.zh: 好老师把抽象理论与学生每天遇到的问题联系起来。

ex.en: Scientists have established a connection between cholesterol levels and heart disease.
ex.zh: 科学家已证实胆固醇含量与心脏病之间有关联。

ex.en: There is a strong connection between sleep quality and mental health.
ex.zh: 睡眠质量与心理健康之间有很强的联系。

ex.en: The train was delayed, and we missed our connection to Paris.
ex.zh: 火车晚点，我们错过了去巴黎的中转班次。

ex.en: While eye contact may be a sign of connection or trust in friendly situations, it's more likely to be associated with dominance or intimidation in adversarial situations.
ex.zh: 虽然眼神交会在友好的环境中可能表示联系或信任，但是在对立的环境中，它更有可能被人与支配或威胁联系到一起。

senses: v. （尤指比赛、赛跑等中）击败，战胜；克服
conquer.usage: [族]conqueror n.征服者；占领者；胜利者；[近]overcome vt.克服；派生conqueror征服者；con(都，一起)+quer(发音似"克")→都攻克了→战胜；征服；索引p405

ex.en: The Normans conquered England in 1066.
ex.zh: 诺曼人于1066年征服了英格兰。

ex.en: She finally conquered her fear of public speaking through constant practice.
ex.zh: 通过不断练习，她终于克服了当众讲话的恐惧。

ex.en: Modern medicine has conquered many diseases that were once fatal.
ex.zh: 现代医学已经战胜了许多曾经致命的疾病。

ex.en: The team conquered every obstacle and reached the summit on schedule.
ex.zh: 团队克服了所有障碍，按计划登上了山顶。

conquest.usage: 辨析:conquest强调征服控制对手;triumph决定性胜利及喜悦心态;victory比赛斗争中击败对手的胜利；conquer 的派生词

ex.en: He continued to expand his kingdom by conquest.
ex.zh: 他通过征服手段继续扩张他的王国。

conscience.usage: to have a good/guilty conscience问心无愧/有愧;助记:con+sci(知道)+ence→良知；n.良知，良心；内疚，愧疚；从事科学（science）事业的科学家们是很有良知（conscience）的。；串词记忆：科学家(scientist)做科学(science)一定要有良知(consc

ex.en: This is an issue of equality, opportunity and national conscience.
ex.zh: 这是一个关于平等、机会和国家良知的问题。

ex.en: Mental health has commonly been called conscience, instinct, wisdom, common sense, or the inner voice.
ex.zh: 心理健康通常被描述成良知、本能、明智、常识或内心的声音。

ex.en: His conscience would not allow him to ignore the suffering of the workers.
ex.zh: 他的良心不允许他无视工人的苦难。

ex.en: She had a clear conscience, having reported the error as soon as she found it.
ex.zh: 她一发现错误就立即上报，因此问心无愧。

senses: adj. 认真的,勤勤恳恳的
conscientious.usage: 派生conscientiousness认真;conscientiously认真地；adj.认真的，勤勤恳恳的；凭 良心的

ex.en: A conscientious worker checks every detail before submitting the final report.
ex.zh: 认真尽责的员工在提交最终报告前会核对每个细节。

ex.en: She is conscientious about answering every customer message within a day.
ex.zh: 她认真负责，坚持在一天之内回复每条顾客留言。

ex.en: Doctors must be conscientious in recording patients' medical histories.
ex.zh: 医生必须认真负责地记录病人的病史。

senses: adj. ①神志清醒的，有……意识的
adj. 注意到，意识到；有知觉的，有意识的
adj. 意识到的；（尤指由于不满或自觉重要而）注意的；有意的；有知觉的
conscious.usage: conscious 指有意识的、自觉的，只强调心理意识的感觉；aware 强调通过耳闻目睹认识到外界存在某事物，通常作表语；词根:con(together一起)+sci(know知道)+ous→知道的→意识到的;②adj.有意的(2011年翻译):In fact, circumstances seem to be de

ex.en: He was conscious that he was talking too much with the stranger.
ex.zh: 他意识到他和这个陌生人说得实在太多了。

ex.en: This forces users to be more conscious of their role in passing along information.
ex.zh: 这要求用户更加留意自己在信息传递中所扮演的角色。

ex.en: The patient remained conscious throughout the operation.
ex.zh: 病人在整个手术过程中始终保持清醒。

ex.en: Young consumers are increasingly conscious of the environmental impact of their purchases.
ex.zh: 年轻消费者越来越意识到自己的购买行为对环境的影响。

ex.en: Many consumers now consciously avoid brands associated with exploitative labour practices.
ex.zh: 如今许多消费者会有意识地避开与剥削性劳工行为相关的品牌。

senses: n. 意识（或觉察）；知觉；（对特定主题或观点的）关注；观念；想法

ex.en: In people who score high in a test of neuroticism, a personality dimension associated with self-consciousness and anxiety, eye contact triggered more activity associated with avoidance.
ex.zh: 神经质是一种与自我意识和焦虑相关的人格维度，在神经质测试得分高的人身上，眼神交流引发了更多与回避相关的举动。

ex.en: Environmental consciousness has grown rapidly among younger consumers.
ex.zh: 年轻消费者的环保意识迅速增强。

ex.en: The patient slowly regained consciousness two days after the operation.
ex.zh: 病人在手术后两天才慢慢恢复知觉。

senses: adj. 连续的,串联的,连贯的
consecutive.usage: con-（一起）+secut（跟随）→一个跟一个→连续的。近义：successive a. 连续的；助记:con(共同)+secut(跟随)+ive→接踵而至的→连续的

ex.en: The hospital has reported record admissions for the third consecutive month.
ex.zh: 该医院连续第三个月报告入院人数创纪录。

senses: n. 共识；（意见等的）一致
n. 共识，（意见等的）一致
consensus.usage: con-（共同）+sens（感觉）→共同的感觉→共识。近义：agreement n. 一致；n.一致看法，共识；con(共同)+sens(联想成sense"感觉")+us(我们)→我们有共同的感觉→共识；consensus 常与 reach/achieve 搭配。；索引p405

ex.en: The consensus among economists is that immigration should not be encouraged.
ex.zh: 移民不应该被鼓励是经济学家们的共识。

ex.en: The parties reached a consensus on environmental policy.
ex.zh: 各党派就环境政策达成了共识。

senses: v. & n. 同意；准许；允许
n. 同意；准许；正式批准文件
consent.usage: 辨析:consent接to;assent赞同提议,接to;comply遵照,接with;abide遵守,接by;反义dissent；n.许可，允许；同意 v.赞同，准许，同意；con(所有)+sent(感觉)→所有人都有同样的感觉→同意；赞同；指同意别人的请求、建议或满足他人的愿望；索引p405

ex.en: There are lessons about informed patient consent to learn.
ex.zh: 在患者知情同意方面，有很多教训可以汲取。

ex.en: No personal data may be collected without the explicit consent of the user.
ex.zh: 未经用户明确同意，不得收集个人数据。

consequence.usage: con-(共同)+sequ(跟随)→随之而来→后果；[族] consequently；[近] result, outcome；n.结果，后果；重要性，价值；易混辨析：多指某一事件引起的不良结果，侧重事件发展的逻辑关系；索引p405

ex.en: Parents have spent years raising us up. As a consequence, they should be supported when they are getting old.
ex.zh: 父母经历那么多年养育我们长大，所以当他们老去的时候，我们应该赡养他们。

ex.en: It is too easy, and misleading, to see such court rulings as merely standing up for the rights of land owners when the consequences can be so dire for their neighbors.
ex.zh: 把这样的法院裁决仅仅看作是为了维护土地所有者的权利，这过于简单且具有误导性，因为对他们的邻居来说，这些裁决的后果可能会很糟。

ex.en: Cutting the training budget may save money now, but the long-term consequences could be severe.
ex.zh: 削减培训预算或许现在能省钱，但长期后果可能很严重。

consequent.usage: adj.随之发生的，作为结果的

consequently.usage: con(表示"所有的")+sequent(表示"连续")→所有的连续都结束了，"因此"下面就没有了→因此，所以；索引p405

ex.en: She was a bright and eager student and, consequently, did well in school.
ex.zh: 她是个聪明好学的学生，因此学习成绩很好。

ex.en: Complex international, economic, technological and cultural changes could start to diminish the leading position of English as the language of the world market, and UK interests which enjoy advantage from the breadth of English usage would consequently face new pressures.
ex.zh: 复杂的国际、经济、技术和文化变化可能开始削弱英语在全球语言中的主导地位，因英语的广泛使用而享有优势的英国各方利益集团将因此面临诸多新压力。

ex.en: The bridge was closed for repairs and, consequently, traffic in the city doubled.
ex.zh: 大桥因维修关闭，因此市内车流量翻了一番。

ex.en: Firms cut investment during the recession and consequently hired far fewer graduates.
ex.zh: 企业在经济衰退期间削减投资，因此招聘的毕业生少得多。

senses: n. 保存，保护，避免损失
conservation.usage: [族] conserve vt. 保护；保存；[族] conserve vt. 保护；n.保护，保存；节约；易混辨析：conservation 由 conserve 派生，指保护或节约；conversation 由 converse 派生，指谈话、交谈；索引p405

ex.en: In effect, fewer federal funds today are going towards the agency's other work—such as forest conservation, watershed and cultural resources management, and infrastructure upkeep—that affect the lives of all Americans.
ex.zh: 实际上，如今用于这个机构（林务局）其他方面工作的联邦资金越来越少——比如说森林保护、集水区、文化资源管理和基础设施维护——而这些工作对所有美国人的生活都会产生影响。

ex.en: The society raises money for the conservation of historic buildings in the old town.
ex.zh: 该协会为保护老城区的历史建筑筹集资金。

ex.en: Energy conservation at home can lower bills and reduce carbon emissions at the same time.
ex.zh: 家庭节约能源既能降低账单开支，又能减少碳排放。

senses: n. （英国）保守党党员，保守的人
[C-]（英国）保守党的；低于实际数量的
conservative.usage: 词根：con(together一起)+serv(keep保持)+ative形容词后缀→保守的；索引p405

ex.en: Its Campaign to Protect Rural England struck terror into many local Conservative parties.
ex.zh: 它（指独立党）的“保护田园英国运动”让很多当地的保守党人感到畏惧。

ex.en: The bank gave a conservative estimate of next year's profits, expecting only modest growth.
ex.zh: 银行对明年利润作了保守估计，预计只有温和增长。

ex.en: Older consumers tend to be more conservative in their choice of brands.
ex.zh: 年长的消费者在品牌选择上往往更为保守。

senses: v. 保护，保存，保藏；节省；节约
conserve.usage: v.保护，保存；节省，节约 n.蜜饯，果脯；con表示“所有的”，你们所有人都去我家做客，我要为你们所有人服务，所以我要提前储备一些食物→保存，保藏。

ex.en: Simple measures, such as repairing leaking taps, can conserve surprising quantities of water.
ex.zh: 修理漏水水龙头这类简单措施能节约数量惊人的水。

senses: vt. 注视；端详；体谅；考虑到；顾及

ex.en: The Supreme Court will now consider whether police can search the contents of a mobile phone without a warrant if the phone is on or around a person during an arrest.
ex.zh: 现在最高法院将考虑以下这种情况：警方在逮捕过程中，如果嫌犯的手机开着或就在嫌犯身边，在没有搜查令的情况下警方能否搜查手机中的内容。

ex.en: Lawmakers must consider the long-term costs of the infrastructure plan.
ex.zh: 立法者必须考虑这项基础设施计划的长期成本。

ex.en: The committee considered her application carefully before granting the scholarship.
ex.zh: 委员会在授予奖学金之前仔细审议了她的申请。

senses: adj. 相当大(多)的，可观的
adj. 相当大（或多、重要等）的
considerable.usage: 发音类似“看谁的萝卜”→看看这是谁家的萝卜，堆在这里堵路了→相当大的，相当多的。；索引p405

ex.en: The industry also points out that real grass require considerable amounts of water.
ex.zh: 该行业还指出，种植真草需要大量的水。

ex.en: The project required considerable investment but generated few visible returns in its first year.
ex.zh: 该项目需要相当大的投资，但第一年几乎没有产生明显回报。

ex.en: The new policy has attracted considerable attention from employers across the country.
ex.zh: 新政策引起了全国各地雇主的极大关注。

ex.en: The revised estimates suggest the project will cost considerably more than the original budget allowed.
ex.zh: 修订后的估算表明，该项目的成本将大大超出原预算。

senses: a. 体贴的；考虑周到的
adj. 考虑周到的，体谅的
adj. 体贴的，考虑周到的
considerate.usage: adj.体贴的；考虑周到的；adj.体贴的，考虑周到的

ex.en: She is always polite and considerate towards her employees.
ex.zh: 她对待雇员总是客客气气，关心体谅。

ex.en: It was considerate of him to warn the neighbours before starting the repairs.
ex.zh: 他动工之前先提醒了邻居，真是体贴。

ex.en: A considerate manager adjusts deadlines when a colleague is clearly overloaded.
ex.zh: 体贴的管理者会在同事明显超负荷时调整截止期限。

ex.en: Please be considerate of other passengers and keep your phone calls brief.
ex.zh: 请体谅其他乘客，尽量缩短通话时间。

senses: n. 仔细考虑；深思；斟酌
n. 考虑；必须考虑的事；关心
consideration.usage: n.考虑；考虑因素；体贴；索引p405

ex.en: Cost is an important consideration when choosing between the two designs.
ex.zh: 在两种设计之间作选择时，成本是重要的考虑因素。

ex.en: The proposal is currently under consideration by the planning committee.
ex.zh: 该提案目前正在规划委员会的审议之中。

ex.en: He showed great consideration for the families affected by the delay.
ex.zh: 他对受延误影响的家庭表现出极大的体谅。

consist.usage: 同义: comprise, include；v.由……组成；在于，存在 于；v.由……组成；在于；con（表示“所有的”）+sist（站）→所有的人都站在这儿→组成，构成；词根记忆：con(together, 一起)+sist(stand, 站)→站在一起→由…组成；索引p405

ex.en: It consists of approximately 75 buildings.
ex.zh: 它由大约75座建筑物组成。

ex.en: Indeed, while you might assume that an exhibition of Land Art would consist only of records of works rather than the works themselves, Long's photograph of his work is the work.
ex.zh: 确实，人们可能以为地景艺术展览的只是作品记录，而非作品本身，但是朗工作的照片就是其作品。

ex.en: True happiness consists not in wealth but in meaningful relationships.
ex.zh: 真正的幸福不在于财富，而在于有意义的人际关系。

senses: a. 一致的；始终如一的
adj. (论点、看法、行为、标准)前后一致的,始终如一的
adj. (with)与……一致的,相符的,不矛盾的
adj. 连续的；一贯的，一致的，相等的
adj. 一致的；始终如一的；持续的
consistent.usage: adj.一贯的；持续的;一致 的；con（表示“所有的”）+sist（站）+ent（形容词后缀，表状态）→站在一起的状态，动作整齐连贯→连续的，一致的。派生：consistently；inconsistent；索引p405

ex.en: They lack consistent support from peers.
ex.zh: 他们缺乏同行的一致支持。

ex.en: While all of these countries face their own challenges, there are a number of consistent themes.
ex.zh: 尽管所有这些国家都面临各自的一些问题，还是有一些一致的主题。

ex.en: Her account of the evening is consistent with the security camera footage.
ex.zh: 她对当晚的叙述与监控录像相符。

senses: adv. 一致地，一贯地；始终一样

ex.en: Her work has been of a consistently high standard.
ex.zh: 她的工作一直是高水准的。

senses: vt. 安慰,抚慰,慰问(某人)
n. (机器、电子设备等的)控制台,仪表板
console.usage: 发音类似“可瘦了”→“我可瘦了，你只是在安慰我”。

ex.en: Nothing could console him when his wife died.
ex.zh: 他妻子去世后，什么事情也不能使他感到宽慰。

consolidate.usage: 派生consolidation巩固;联合;助记:con(共同)+solid(坚实的)+ate(使...)→使坚实→巩固；con（所有的，共同）+solid（结实的，固体）+ate（动词后缀）→都很结实→巩固，加强。；索引p405

ex.en: The popularity of these novels consolidated Dickens' as a nationally and internationally celebrated man of letters.
ex.zh: 这些小说的流行巩固了狄更斯作为国内外著名文人的地位。

ex.en: Cooper and her colleagues argue that a "town of culture" award could consolidate the town-city ties in Britain.
ex.zh: 库珀和她的同事认为，“文化城镇”奖可以加强英国城镇之间的联系。

ex.en: The merger allowed the two airlines to consolidate their routes and cut operating costs.
ex.zh: 这次合并使两家航空公司得以整合航线并削减运营成本。

senses: adj. 显眼的,明显的,引人注目的
adj. 明显的，引人注目的
conspicuous.usage: 同义obvious,prominent,outstanding;助记:con+spicu(看)+ous→能引起共同观看的→显眼的；adj.引人注目的；显眼的，明 显的；con（表示“所有人”）+spic（看）+uous（……的）→所有人都看得到的→明显的，引人注目的

ex.en: The advertisements were all posted in a conspicuous place.
ex.zh: 广告都贴在了显眼的地方。

ex.en: The new tower is conspicuous among the city's low wooden houses.
ex.zh: 在这座城市低矮的木屋中间，新塔楼十分显眼。

ex.en: He was conspicuous by his absence from the annual shareholders' meeting.
ex.zh: 他未出席年度股东大会，格外引人注意。

senses: n. 阴谋活动(尤指共谋犯罪)

ex.en: The executives were charged with conspiracy to fix fuel prices.
ex.zh: 这些高管被控合谋操纵燃油价格。

ex.en: Conspiracy theories spread faster than corrections on social media.
ex.zh: 阴谋论在社交媒体上比辟谣信息传播得更快。

ex.en: Investigators uncovered a conspiracy between officials and building contractors.
ex.zh: 调查人员揭露了官员与建筑承包商之间的密谋。

senses: v. (事件)凑在一起致使,共同导致

ex.en: Critics joked that bad luck and poor planning seemed to conspire against the project from the outset.
ex.zh: 批评者打趣说，坏运气和糟糕的规划似乎从一开始就联合起来跟这个项目作对。

senses: n. (英国最低级别的)警察;保安官
n. 恒久不变;稳定;忠诚;忠实

ex.en: The lighthouse's constancy through a century of storms made it a symbol of the town's endurance.
ex.zh: 这座灯塔在百年风暴中始终如一，成为小镇坚韧精神的象征。

senses: adj. 坚定的,永恒的,忠实的
adj. 不变的；连续不断的
adj. 固定的；连续发生的
constant.usage: 辨析: constant 持续的、不变的、忠实的; continual 频繁的、时断时续,常指不愉快的事; continuous (时间、空间上)连续不断的; 反义: changeable；adj.持续不断的，经常的；恒定 的 n.常数；不变的事物；con(表示"都，所有的")+stant(=stand，表示"站")→

ex.en: Vanity is a constant; people will only start shopping more sustainably when they can't afford not to.
ex.zh: 虚荣心是永恒不变的；人们只有在负担不起的时候才会开始可持续性购物。

ex.en: Newport also recommends "deep scheduling" to combat constant interruptions and get more done in less time.
ex.zh: 纽波特还推荐采用"深度计划"来对抗接连不断的干扰，并提高工作效率。

ex.en: The machine requires constant attention, since a brief failure could halt the whole line.
ex.zh: 这台机器需要持续的关注，因为短暂故障就可能使整条生产线停工。

senses: adv. 始终,一直,重复不断地
adv. 连续不断地；始终，一直
constantly.usage: adv.总是，经常地，不断地；索引p405

ex.en: The language is constantly evolving as new words enter everyday use.
ex.zh: 随着新词进入日常使用，语言在不断发展变化。

ex.en: Nurses constantly monitor the patient's heart rate during the operation.
ex.zh: 手术期间，护士持续监测病人的心率。

ex.en: Small businesses constantly struggle to keep up with changing regulations.
ex.zh: 小企业一直在艰难地跟上不断变化的法规。

constituent.usage: 记：con-(共同)+stitu(建立)+-ent→共同建立而成→组成的；[族]constitutive a.组成部分的；[近]element n.成分；n.选民；成分 adj.组成的，构成的；索引p405

ex.en: the needs of the constituents
ex.zh: 选民的需求

ex.en: Hydrogen and oxygen are the basic constituents of water.
ex.zh: 氢和氧是水的基本成分。

ex.en: Senators spend considerable time answering letters from their constituents.
ex.zh: 参议员花费大量时间回复选民的来信。

ex.en: Trust is a constituent element of any successful partnership.
ex.zh: 信任是任何成功伙伴关系的组成要素。

senses: v. 组成，构成；设立，成立；被算作，（被认为或看作）是
constitute.usage: [族] constitution n. 宪法；组成；同义: form, organize, compose, establish；con（表示“一起”）+stitut（=stand“站”）+e→站到了一起→组成，构成。；索引p405

ex.en: Women constitute nearly half of the workforce in this industry.
ex.zh: 女性约占该行业劳动力的一半。

ex.en: Repeated delays in payment may constitute a breach of the original agreement.
ex.zh: 一再拖延付款可能构成对原协议的违反。

ex.en: The new rules constitute a major change in how universities admit overseas students.
ex.zh: 新规定是大学录取海外学生方式的一项重大变化。

senses: n. 宪法；构造；身体素质
constitution.usage: n.宪法，章程；体质； 组成，结构；索引p405

ex.en: Just how much does the Constitution protect your digital data?
ex.zh: 宪法究竟能为你的数字化信息提供多大程度的保护呢？

ex.en: The new constitution guarantees freedom of speech and of the press.
ex.zh: 新宪法保障言论自由和新闻自由。

ex.en: Only a strong constitution allowed him to work such long hours.
ex.zh: 只有强健的体格才能让他每天工作这么长时间。

ex.en: Judges must interpret the constitution in the light of modern conditions.
ex.zh: 法官必须根据现代情况解释宪法。

senses: adj. 宪法的,有宪法权力的

ex.en: The court ruled that the search violated constitutional protections of privacy.
ex.zh: 法院裁定这次搜查违反了宪法对隐私的保护。

ex.en: Critics questioned whether the emergency powers were constitutional.
ex.zh: 批评者质疑这些紧急权力是否符合宪法。

ex.en: The country adopted a new constitutional framework after decades of military rule.
ex.zh: 该国在数十年军人统治之后通过了新的宪法框架。

ex.en: The judges are still debating the constitutionality of the new tax.
ex.zh: 法官们仍在辩论这项新税是否符合宪法。

ex.en: Opponents have challenged the constitutionality of the travel ban in court.
ex.zh: 反对者已在法庭上对旅行禁令的合宪性提出质疑。

ex.en: The government defended the constitutionality of its emergency measures.
ex.zh: 政府为其紧急措施的合宪性进行了辩护。

senses: vt. 强制,迫使,强迫(某人)做某事
v. 限制，约束；强迫，迫使
constrain.usage: 记：con-(加强意义)+strain(束缚)→用条条框框束缚某人→限制；[族]constraint n.限制；[近]restrict vt.限制；con（表示加强）+strain（拉紧）→使劲拉紧→强迫，迫使；词根记忆：con(together,共同)+strain(draw tight,拉紧)→共同拉紧的行为→强迫

ex.en: constrain the ability
ex.zh: 限制能力

ex.en: The company said that it was constrained to raise prices.
ex.zh: 该公司说它被迫提高价格。

ex.en: Men and women are becoming less constrained by stereotyped roles.
ex.zh: 男性和女性越来越不受陈规定型角色的束缚。

ex.en: A lack of formal education, however, doesn't constrain the ability of the developing world's workforce to substantially improve productivity for the foreseeable future.
ex.zh: 然而，发展中国家的劳动力在可预见的未来持续提高生产率的能力没有因缺乏正规教育而受到限制。

senses: n. 约束,限制;强迫,强制

ex.en: financial constraints
ex.zh: 财政约束

ex.en: Time constraints forced the team to simplify the original design.
ex.zh: 时间限制迫使团队简化了最初的设计。

ex.en: The researchers worked within the constraints of a very limited budget.
ex.zh: 研究人员在极为有限的预算约束下开展工作。

ex.en: Legal constraints prevent the agency from publishing the names of witnesses.
ex.zh: 法律限制使该机构不能公布证人的姓名。

senses: n. [C]复杂的构想（或思想）；观念
n. 构想,概念,观念;结构体,建造物
construct.usage: 记：con-(加强意义)+struct(建造)→建造；[族]construction n.建造；[近]concept n.观念；v.建造，修建；组成；绘制 n.构想，观念；词根记忆: con(together, 共同)+struct(build, 建造)→建造；真 In plays, novels and narrat

ex.en: construct executive offices
ex.zh: 建造行政办公室

ex.en: The first executive offices were constructed between 1799 and 1820.
ex.zh: 第一批行政办公楼建于1799年至1820年之间。

ex.en: Engineers constructed a temporary bridge within seventy-two hours.
ex.zh: 工程人员在七十二小时内建成了一座临时桥梁。

ex.en: The theory was constructed from years of careful field observation.
ex.zh: 这一理论是在多年细致的实地观察基础上构建的。

senses: n. 建造；建筑物；建筑业；创立
construction.usage: n.建造；创立，构建；建筑物；n.建造，建筑；创立；索引p405

ex.en: Construction of the new airport will create thousands of temporary jobs.
ex.zh: 新机场的建设将创造数千个临时就业岗位。

ex.en: The bridge remained closed for two years during construction.
ex.zh: 大桥在施工期间关闭了两年。

ex.en: The construction industry suffered badly when public investment was cut.
ex.zh: 公共投资削减后，建筑业遭受重创。

senses: adj. 建设性的；积极性的

consult.usage: 派生consultation商量,商讨,商议;助记:con(一起)+sult(召集)→商议；形近对照法：你查阅（consult）了所有的资料，但还是没找到结果（result）。；查阅（consult）了各种资料，但依然没有结果（result）。；索引p405

ex.en: I need to consult with my colleagues on the proposals.
ex.zh: 我需要和我的同事商讨这些建议。

ex.en: Patients are encouraged to consult a doctor before starting any demanding exercise program.
ex.zh: 鼓励患者在开始任何高强度锻炼计划前咨询医生。

ex.en: You can consult the appendix for a full list of the sources cited.
ex.zh: 你可以查阅附录，获取所引文献的完整清单。

senses: n. 咨询公司；专家咨询
consultancy.usage: n.咨询公司；咨询意见，顾问 工作；索引p405

ex.en: She joined a management consultancy after finishing her economics degree.
ex.zh: 读完经济学学位后，她加入了一家管理咨询公司。

ex.en: The firm offers consultancy services to hospitals seeking to cut waiting times.
ex.zh: 该公司为希望缩短等候时间的医院提供咨询服务。

ex.en: His consultancy employs over two hundred analysts in London alone.
ex.zh: 他的咨询公司仅在伦敦就雇用了两百多名分析师。

phrases.m: 心脏外科高级顾问医师

consultant.usage: 记：consult（仔细考虑）+-ant（名词后缀）→能提供专业意见的人→顾问；派生consultancy咨询公司;专家咨询；n.顾问；高级顾问医师，会诊 医师；咨询者；索引p405

ex.en: The firm hired a management consultant to identify sources of waste in its supply chain.
ex.zh: 该公司聘请了一位管理顾问，以找出供应链中的浪费环节。

ex.en: As a senior consultant, she advises hospitals on how to shorten their waiting lists.
ex.zh: 作为一名资深顾问医师，她为医院提供缩短候诊名单的建议。

ex.en: The consultant's report blamed poor communication rather than lack of funding.
ex.zh: 顾问的报告将问题归咎于沟通不畅，而非资金不足。

consultation.usage: n.磋商会议；咨询，就诊；查 阅

senses: v. 消耗，消费；吃，喝；使充满
consume.usage: [族] consumer n. 消费者；consumption n. 消耗；消费量；vt.消耗，消费 vi.耗尽；耗尽生命；adj.（感情）强烈的，支配人的；都（con）输（su）我（me），比赛时，都输给我了，肯定是精力和体力都“消耗”完了。派生：consumer；consumption；索引p405

ex.en: Some scientists claim that people should consume the right kind of food at breakfast.
ex.zh: 一些科学家声称，人们应该在早餐时摄入合适的食物。

ex.en: They found that the aircraft consumed as much as 15% less fuel (coupled with a reduction in carbon-dioxide output).
ex.zh: 他们发现飞机节省了多达15%的燃油(相应的二氧化碳排放量也减少了)。

ex.en: From 1998 to 2000, 14.5 percent of the fruit Americans consumed was imported.
ex.zh: 自1998年到2000年间，美国人食用的水果中有14.5%是进口的。

ex.en: Consumer spending rose sharply during the holiday season.
ex.zh: 假日季消费者支出大幅上升。

ex.en: Regulators promised to protect consumer interests in the merger review.
ex.zh: 监管机构承诺在此次合并审查中保护消费者利益。

ex.en: Digital technology has shifted bargaining power towards the consumer.
ex.zh: 数字技术使议价能力向消费者转移。

consumerism.usage: n.消费主义，保护消费者利益主义；索引p405

ex.en: The documentary examines how consumerism has reshaped holidays into seasons of shopping.
ex.zh: 这部纪录片审视了消费主义如何把节日变成了购物季。

senses: n. (能量、食物或材料的)消耗，消耗量；消费
consumption.usage: n.消费、消耗；consume 的派生词；索引p405

ex.en: They use their money reserves to back up consumption.
ex.zh: 他们用自己的货币储备来支持消费。

ex.en: The government aims to cut energy consumption in public buildings by a third.
ex.zh: 政府力争将公共建筑的能耗削减三分之一。

ex.en: Doctors advise moderate consumption of red meat.
ex.zh: 医生建议适量食用红肉。

ex.en: Rising domestic consumption has become the main engine of the country's growth.
ex.zh: 不断增长的国内消费已成为该国增长的主要引擎。

contact.usage: 记：con-（加强意义）+tact（接触）→接触；词组bring into/throw in contact with使接触;come in/to contact with接触,碰上;have contact with接触到;同义touch,connect,approach；n.联络；接触；熟人 v.联系，联络；con

ex.en: Personality can affect how a person reacts to eye contact.
ex.zh: 个性会影响一个人对目光接触的反应。

ex.en: However, the Justices said that Arizona police would be allowed to verify the legal status of people who come in contact with law enforcement.
ex.zh: 然而，法官们说，亚利桑那州的警察将被允许去核实与执法部门接触的人的法律地位。

ex.en: Please contact the service center if the device fails to start within thirty seconds.
ex.zh: 如果设备三十秒内无法启动，请联系服务中心。

senses: adj. (疾病)接触传染的;患接触传染病的
adj. (感情、态度、行动)富于感染力的,会蔓延的
v. 包含,容纳;相当于;折合
vt. 包含；抑制（感情）；防止…蔓延
contain.usage: 记：con-（加强意义）+tain（握）→手中握有很多东西→含有；同义hold,include,comprise;control,restrain;派生containment n.包含;控制；v.包含，容纳；遏制；易混辨析：contain为普通用词，强调包容关系，既可指具体有形的东西，也可指抽象无形的东西；索引p405

ex.en: Surveys and test samples have also become important for understanding the larger landscapes that contain archaeological sites.
ex.zh: 勘测和抽样分析对于了解包含考古遗址在内的更大范围的地貌特征也十分重要。

ex.en: The report contains several recommendations on how to reduce traffic congestion.
ex.zh: 报告包含几条关于如何减少交通拥堵的建议。

ex.en: Firefighters managed to contain the blaze before it reached the warehouse.
ex.zh: 消防员在大火蔓延到仓库之前控制住了火势。

ex.en: Fresh vegetables contain vitamins that are easily destroyed by overcooking.
ex.zh: 新鲜蔬菜所含的维生素很容易因过度烹煮而被破坏。

ex.en: Global trade depends on standard containers that fit any ship or train.
ex.zh: 全球贸易依赖可用于任何船舶或列车的标准集装箱。

ex.en: Store the chemicals in a sealed container away from direct sunlight.
ex.zh: 把这些化学品存放在避免阳光直射的密封容器中。

ex.en: Start-up companies are turning old shipping containers into affordable offices.
ex.zh: 初创公司正把旧海运集装箱改造成价格亲民的办公室。

contaminate.usage: 助记:con(共同,全部)+tamin(接触)+ate(动词后缀)→全部都被坏东西接触了→污染;派生contamination n.污染

ex.en: The drinking water has become contaminated with lead.
ex.zh: 饮用水被铅污染了。

senses: v. 冥思(某事物)(尤指宗教仪式)；沉思，考虑
contemplate.usage: 近义：consider v. 考虑；发音类似"看它不累的"→看着一个东西陷入了深思，都忘记了累→沉思，深思熟虑；索引p405

ex.en: The government has contemplated reforming the entire tax system.
ex.zh: 政府打算改革整个税收体制。

ex.en: The thought of holding a fixed grin as the camera performed its magical duties was too much to contemplate, and so a non-committal blank stare became the norm.
ex.zh: 当相机履行它的神奇职能时，一想到要保持固定的微笑，简直不敢想象，因此面无表情、茫然凝视成了标准姿态。

ex.en: The board is contemplating a merger with its largest competitor.
ex.zh: 董事会正在考虑与最大的竞争对手合并。

ex.en: He sat by the lake, contemplating the changes in his life.
ex.zh: 他坐在湖边，沉思着自己生活中的种种变化。

senses: a. 同一时代的；属同时期的
adj. 同时代的,同时发生的
n. 同代人,(几乎)同年龄的人
contemporary.usage: 记：con-(共同)+tempor(时间)+-ary(形后缀)→同一时间共同经历变化→同一时代的；[族]contemporaneous a.同时代的；[近]modern a.当代的；辨析: contemporary 当代的或同时代的; modern 现代的、近代的,与 ancient, medieval 相对；adj.

ex.en: sales of contemporary art
ex.zh: 当代艺术品的销售额

ex.en: Sales of contemporary art fell by two-thirds, and in the most overheated sector, they were down by nearly 90% in the year to November 2008.
ex.zh: 截至2008年11月，当代艺术品的销售额下降了三分之二，在最热门的领域，销售额则下降了近90%。

ex.en: In our contemporary culture, the prospect of communicating with—or even looking at—a stranger is virtually unbearable.
ex.zh: 在我们当代的文化(观念)中，同一个陌生人交流，甚至只是看他们一眼都是让人无法忍受的。

senses: n. [U,sing.]（对规则、危险等的）藐视，不顾
n. (对规则、危险等的)蔑视,毫不畏惧
n. 轻视，轻蔑；藐视，不顾
contempt.usage: 记：con-(加强)+tempt(藐视)→藐视他人的行为→轻蔑；[族]contemptible a.可鄙的卑劣的；[近]scorn n.鄙视；同义: scorn, dishonor; 反义: respect；n.轻视，蔑视；忽视，不顾； 藐视法庭；联想记忆: con(together, 共同)+tempt(try, 尝

ex.en: earn the contempt of sb.
ex.zh: 遭到某人的鄙视

ex.en: The firefighters showed a contempt for their own safety.
ex.zh: 那些消防队员已把他们自己的安全置之度外。

ex.en: "So few authors have brains enough or literary gift enough to keep their own end up in journalism," Newman wrote, "that I am tempted to define 'journalism' as 'a term of contempt applied by writers who are not read to writers who are'."
ex.zh: 纽曼写道，“很少有作家能拥有足够的智慧或文学天分以保证他们能在新闻写作中有所作为，以至于我想把‘新闻写作’定义为‘不受欢迎的作家用于嘲弄受读者欢迎的作家的不敬之词’”。

ex.en: Deliberately spreading false health advice for profit is widely regarded as contemptible conduct.
ex.zh: 为牟利而故意散布虚假健康建议被广泛视为可鄙的行为。

ex.en: The court was contemptuous of McDonnell's conduct.
ex.zh: 法院对麦克唐纳的行为表示鄙视。

ex.en: The judge was openly contemptuous of the defendant's excuses.
ex.zh: 法官对被告的辩解表示出公开的蔑视。

ex.en: He gave a contemptuous glance at the tabloid headlines.
ex.zh: 他轻蔑地瞥了一眼那些小报标题。

senses: vi. （尤指在争论中）声称；竞争
contend.usage: 记：con-(共同)+tend(伸)→共同将手伸向某物→争夺；[族]contender n.竞争者；[近]compete vi.竞争；v.声称，主张；竞争，争 夺；处理，对付；索引p405

ex.en: contend that
ex.zh: 声称

ex.en: It is the playgoers, the RSC contends, who bring in much of the town's revenue.
ex.zh: 皇家莎士比亚剧团认为，是看戏的人给小镇带来了大部分的收入。

ex.en: But in her new book, Join the Club, Tina Rosenberg contends that peer pressure can also be a positive force through what she calls the social cure.
ex.zh: 但是蒂娜·罗森伯格在其新书《加入俱乐部》中指出，同辈压力也可能通过她称之为“社会救治”的活动而成为正面力量。

senses: n. (pl.)内容,目录;(书、文章等的)主题,要旨;(网站的)信息内容
content.usage: 记：con-（加强意义）+tent（握）→握住某人的手表示某个结果，很符合自己心意→满意的；词根记忆:con(together,共同)+ten(hold,握,持有)→共同持有→内容;名词读'kɒntent,形容词读kən'tent；索引p405

ex.en: The test contents and formats for adults and children may be different.
ex.zh: 成人和儿童的考试内容和形式可能不同。

ex.en: The content of the examination has changed little in twenty years.
ex.zh: 二十年来，考试内容几乎没有变化。

ex.en: After a simple meal by the fire, they sat content and silent.
ex.zh: 在火边吃过一顿简单的饭之后，他们心满意足地静静坐着。

ex.en: Streaming platforms compete to produce original content for their subscribers.
ex.zh: 流媒体平台竞相为订户制作原创内容。

senses: n. 争吵,争执,争论;(尤指争论时的)看法,观点
contention.usage: n.看法，观点；争论，争 吵

ex.en: It is her contention that remote work raises rather than lowers productivity.
ex.zh: 她的观点是，远程办公会提高而不是降低生产率。

ex.en: The boundary of the old farm remains a matter of contention between the two villages.
ex.zh: 旧农场的边界仍是两村之间争执的问题。

ex.en: The main contention of the article is that exams fail to measure creativity.
ex.zh: 这篇文章的主要论点是考试无法衡量创造力。

senses: n. 竞赛,比赛;(控制权或权力的)竞争,争夺
v. 争夺,竞争,争论,就……提出异议
vt. 争辩；争夺赢得（比赛、选举等）

phrases.m: 一场即将举行的歌唱比赛

contest.usage: 同义: fight, struggle, contend；n.比赛，竞赛；竞争 v.争辩，提出异议；争取赢得；词根记忆：con(一起)+test(看到)→一起观看比赛→比赛；索引p405

ex.en: In Arizona v.s. United States, the majority overturned three of the four contested provisions of Arizona's controversial plan to have state and local police enforce federal immigration law.
ex.zh: 在亚利桑那州和美国的对决中，大多数法官推翻了亚利桑那州四条颇具争议的移民法案中的三条，该法案使州警察和地方警察执行联邦移民法。

ex.en: She entered the national essay contest and won first prize.
ex.zh: 她参加了全国征文比赛并获得一等奖。

ex.en: The opposition contested the election results, alleging irregularities in several districts.
ex.zh: 反对派对选举结果提出异议，声称数个选区存在违规行为。

ex.en: The contest for the leadership of the party lasted three months.
ex.zh: 该党领导权的争夺持续了三个月。

phrases.m: 在上下文中 / 脱离上下文,断章取义
在这一点上,在这种情况下

context.usage: 词根记忆：con(together,一起)+text(文本)→很多文本放在一起构成了上下文→语境；索引p405

ex.en: The better you understand the cultural context, the more control you can have over your impact.
ex.zh: 你对文化背景理解得越深刻，你就越能掌控你的影响。

ex.en: Taken out of context, the quotation appears to support the opposite view.
ex.zh: 脱离上下文来看，这段引文似乎支持相反的观点。

ex.en: Students should try to guess the meaning of new words from their context.
ex.zh: 学生应尝试根据上下文猜测生词的意思。

ex.en: The policy can only be understood in the context of the country's history.
ex.zh: 只有结合该国的历史背景才能理解这项政策。

contextual.usage: adj.上下文的，与语境相关的；索引p405

ex.en: Modern translation systems rely on contextual cues to decide which meaning of an ambiguous word applies.
ex.zh: 现代翻译系统依靠上下文线索来判断多义词在此处的具体含义。

senses: vt. 将…置于背景中考虑；将…置于上下文中
n. 大陆；洲；欧洲大陆（不包括英国和爱尔兰）
continent.usage: 哥伦布发现新大陆时，亢（con）奋地踢（ti）那片嫩土（nent），说发现新“大陆”了。

ex.en: The police investigation spanned three continents.
ex.zh: 警方的调查跨越三大洲。

ex.en: Goods now move between factories on one continent and consumers on another.
ex.zh: 如今，货物在一大洲的工厂与另一大洲的消费者之间流动。

ex.en: The disease spread across the continent within a few months.
ex.zh: 这种疾病在几个月内蔓延至整个大洲。

senses: adj. 大洲的；大陆的；欧洲大陆的（不包括英国和爱尔兰）

ex.en: The continental shelf off the northern coast may hold significant reserves of oil and gas.
ex.zh: 北部沿海的大陆架可能蕴藏着可观的油气储量。

senses: n. (志趣相投、尤指来自同一地方的)一组与会者,代表团
contingent.usage: 派生contingently adv.偶发地,临时地；索引p405

ex.en: Payment of the annual bonus is contingent upon the company achieving its published sales targets.
ex.zh: 年度奖金的发放取决于公司是否完成其公布的销售目标。

senses: ②(只用于名词前)(令人厌烦地)反复的，频繁的
continual.usage: adj.多次重复的，频繁的；不 间断的；索引p405

ex.en: The team suffered continual delays caused by the severe weather.
ex.zh: 恶劣天气使团队不断遭遇延误。

ex.en: Continual complaints from neighbours finally forced the factory to cut night work.
ex.zh: 邻居们不断的投诉终于迫使工厂减少夜间作业。

ex.en: Learning a language demands continual practice rather than occasional bursts of effort.
ex.zh: 学习语言需要持续练习，而不是偶尔突击。

ex.en: Residents complained that the construction site continually produced loud noise late at night.
ex.zh: 居民们抱怨工地深夜不断发出巨大的噪音。

ex.en: The judge granted a continuance of the trial because a key witness was unable to appear in court.
ex.zh: 由于一名关键证人无法出庭，法官批准了庭审延期。

senses: vt.&vi. 持续；继续存在；不断发生；继续做
③(中断后)继续，再开始；继续说

ex.en: But as companies continue their attempts at personalized medicine, the courts will remain rather busy.
ex.zh: 但随着公司继续尝试个性化医疗，法院仍将相当忙碌。

ex.en: Salaries are likely to continue rising faster than productivity.
ex.zh: 工资很可能继续以快于生产率的速度上涨。

ex.en: The study will continue until the last participant completes the programme.
ex.zh: 该研究将持续到最后一名参与者完成项目为止。

senses: n. 连续性,持续性;(逻辑上的)连接,联结
n. (电影或电视节目场景中服装、物体等的)一致性,衔接

ex.en: The new director promised continuity rather than radical change.
ex.zh: 新主管承诺保持连续性，而非激进变革。

ex.en: There is little continuity between the two halves of the novel.
ex.zh: 小说的前后两部分之间几乎缺乏连贯性。

ex.en: Constant staff turnover threatens the continuity of patient care.
ex.zh: 员工不断流失威胁到病人护理的连续性。

senses: a. 连续不断的；持续的
a.（线、表面等）连续的，没有间隔的
continuous.usage: 记：con-(加强)+tin(握)+-uous(形后缀)→一直握着没松手→持续的；[族]continuity n.连续性；[近]continual a.接连不断的；索引p405

ex.en: continuous waves of immigrants
ex.zh: 持续不断的移民潮

ex.en: Its continuous supply is becoming a reality.
ex.zh: 它（指清洁能源）的持续供应正在成为现实。

ex.en: The sensor provides a continuous record of temperature changes in the soil.
ex.zh: 该传感器持续记录土壤温度的变化。

senses: v. 缩小,缩短,缩紧;立约规定(或雇佣、承担、执行等)
contract.usage: 同义: agreement, treaty; 反义: expand；n.合同，契约 v.收缩，缩小；签合同；con（所有的）+tract（拽，拉）→一起拽，大家都往有利于自己利益的方向拽，需要一个“合同，契约”。；词根:con(together一起)+tract(draw拉)→一起拉伸肌肉→(使)收缩;②v.(使)收缩

ex.en: Several computer engineers have been contracted to the finance department.
ex.zh: 有几位计算机工程师与财务部门签订了合同。

ex.en: One accounting firm, EY, uses an AI system that helps review contracts during an audit.
ex.zh: 安永会计师事务所使用人工智能系统，在审计期间帮助审查合同。

ex.en: Metals contract in cold weather, which engineers must allow for in bridge design.
ex.zh: 金属在寒冷天气中会收缩，工程师在桥梁设计中必须考虑到这一点。

senses: n. 承包人，承包商；承包公司

ex.en: The council hired an independent contractor to repair the aging bridge before the winter storms arrived.
ex.zh: 议会雇了一家独立承包商，在冬季风暴来临前修理那座老化的大桥。

senses: v. 反驳，驳斥；相矛盾，相抵触
contradict.usage: contra-（相反）+dict（说）→说反话→反驳。族：contradiction n. 矛盾。近义：refute vt. 驳斥；同义: oppose, dispute, conflict; 反义: admit；contra（反对，相反）+dict（说）→反着说→反驳；contradict sb 直接接宾语，不加 t
